cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is an alcohol, and how does a phenol differ from it?
cards.back: An alcohol contains one or more hydroxyl (OH) group(s) directly attached to carbon atom(s), of an aliphatic system (CH3OH) while a phenol contains –OH group(s) directly attached to carbon atom(s) of an aromatic system (C6H5OH).
cards.quote: An alcohol contains one or more hydroxyl (OH) group(s) directly attached to carbon atom(s), of an aliphatic system (CH3OH) while a phenol contains –OH group(s) directly attached to carbon atom(s) of an aromatic system (C6H5OH).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alcohols and phenols are formed when a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon, ____ respectively, is replaced by –OH group.
cards.back: Alcohols and phenols are formed when a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon, aliphatic and aromatic respectively, is replaced by –OH group.
cards.quote: Alcohols and phenols are formed when a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon, aliphatic and aromatic respectively, is replaced by –OH group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are ethers?
cards.back: The substitution of a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon by an alkoxy or aryloxy group (R–O/Ar–O) yields another class of compounds known as ‘ethers’, for example, CH3OCH3 (dimethyl ether).
cards.quote: The substitution of a hydrogen atom in a hydrocarbon by an alkoxy or aryloxy group (R–O/Ar–O) yields another class of compounds known as ‘ethers’, for example, CH3OCH3 (dimethyl ether).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How may ethers be visualised in terms of an alcohol or phenol?
cards.back: You may also visualise ethers as compounds formed by substituting the hydrogen atom of hydroxyl group of an alcohol or phenol by an alkyl or aryl group.
cards.quote: You may also visualise ethers as compounds formed by substituting the hydrogen atom of hydroxyl group of an alcohol or phenol by an alkyl or aryl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Classification of alcohols and phenols by the number of hydroxyl groups?
cards.back: mono–, di–, tri- or polyhydric compounds depending on whether they contain one, two, three or many hydroxyl groups respectively
cards.quote: Alcohols and phenols may be classified as mono–, di–, tri- or polyhydric compounds depending on whether they contain one, two, three or many hydroxyl groups respectively in their structures

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Monohydric alcohols may be further classified according to the ____ of the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl group is attached.
cards.back: Monohydric alcohols may be further classified according to the hybridisation of the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl group is attached.
cards.quote: Monohydric alcohols may be further classified according to the hybridisation of the carbon atom to which the hydroxyl group is attached.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Monohydric alcohols containing a Csp3–OH bond: where is the –OH group attached?
cards.back: In this class of alcohols, the –OH group is attached to an sp3 hybridised carbon atom of an alkyl group.
cards.quote: In this class of alcohols, the –OH group is attached to an sp3 hybridised carbon atom of an alkyl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are allylic alcohols?
cards.back: In these alcohols, the –OH group is attached to a sp3 hybridised carbon adjacent to the carbon-carbon double bond, that is to an allylic carbon.
cards.quote: In these alcohols, the –OH group is attached to a sp3 hybridised carbon adjacent to the carbon-carbon double bond, that is to an allylic carbon.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are benzylic alcohols?
cards.back: In these alcohols, the –OH group is attached to a sp3–hybridised carbon atom next to an aromatic ring.
cards.quote: In these alcohols, the –OH group is attached to a sp3–hybridised carbon atom next to an aromatic ring.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alcohols with a Csp2–OH bond: what are they and what else are they called?
cards.back: These alcohols contain –OH group bonded to a carbon-carbon double bond, i.e., to a vinylic carbon or to an aryl carbon. These alcohols are also known as vinylic alcohols.
cards.quote: These alcohols contain –OH group bonded to a carbon-carbon double bond, i.e., to a vinylic carbon or to an aryl carbon. These alcohols are also known as vinylic alcohols.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the structure of vinylic alcohol?
cards.back: CH2 = CH – OH
cards.quote: Vinylic alcohol: CH2 = CH – OH

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Types of ethers by the groups attached to the oxygen atom?
cards.back:
simple or symmetrical, if the alkyl or aryl groups attached to the oxygen atom are the same
mixed or unsymmetrical, if the two groups are different
cards.quote: Ethers are classified as simple or symmetrical, if the alkyl or aryl groups attached to the oxygen atom are the same, and mixed or unsymmetrical, if the two groups are different.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which of diethyl ether, C2H5OCH3 and C2H5OC6H5 is a symmetrical ether?
cards.back: Diethyl ether, C2H5OC2H5, is a symmetrical ether whereas C2H5OCH3 and C2H5OC6H5 are unsymmetrical ethers.
cards.quote: Diethyl ether, C2H5OC2H5, is a symmetrical ether whereas C2H5OCH3 and C2H5OC6H5 are unsymmetrical ethers.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is the common name of an alcohol derived?
cards.back: The common name of an alcohol is derived from the common name of the alkyl group and adding the word alcohol to it. For example, CH3OH is methyl alcohol.
cards.quote: The common name of an alcohol is derived from the common name of the alkyl group and adding the word alcohol to it. For example, CH3OH is methyl alcohol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is the IUPAC name of an alcohol derived?
cards.back: According to IUPAC system, the name of an alcohol is derived from the name of the alkane from which the alcohol is derived, by substituting ‘e’ of alkane with the suffix ‘ol’.
cards.quote: According to IUPAC system, the name of an alcohol is derived from the name of the alkane from which the alcohol is derived, by substituting ‘e’ of alkane with the suffix ‘ol’.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: For naming polyhydric alcohols, the ‘e’ of alkane is ____ and the ending ‘ol’ is added.
cards.back: For naming polyhydric alcohols, the ‘e’ of alkane is retained and the ending ‘ol’ is added.
cards.quote: For naming polyhydric alcohols, the ‘e’ of alkane is retained and the ending ‘ol’ is added.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The number of –OH groups is indicated by adding the ____, di, tri, etc., before ‘ol’.
cards.back: The number of –OH groups is indicated by adding the multiplicative prefix, di, tri, etc., before ‘ol’.
cards.quote: The number of –OH groups is indicated by adding the multiplicative prefix, di, tri, etc., before ‘ol’.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of HO–CH2–CH2–OH?
cards.back: ethane–1, 2-diol
cards.quote: HO–CH2–CH2–OH is named as ethane–1, 2-diol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.1: common names of ethane-1,2-diol and propane-1,2,3-triol, in that order?
cards.back:
Ethylene glycol
Glycerol
cards.quote: Ethylene glycol Glycerol Ethane-1,2-diol Propane -1, 2, 3-triol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.1: IUPAC names of methyl alcohol, n-propyl alcohol and isopropyl alcohol, in that order?
cards.back:
Methanol
Propan-1-ol
Propan-2-ol
cards.quote: Methyl alcohol n-Propyl alcohol Isopropyl alcohol Methanol Propan-1-ol Propan-2-ol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.1: IUPAC name of tert-butyl alcohol?
cards.back: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol
cards.quote: tert-Butyl alcohol 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.1: IUPAC name of sec-butyl alcohol?
cards.back: Butan-2-ol
cards.quote: sec-Butyl alcohol Butan-2-ol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.1: IUPAC name of isobutyl alcohol?
cards.back: 2-Methylpropan-1-ol
cards.quote: Isobutyl alcohol 2-Methylpropan-1-ol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Cyclic alcohols are named using the prefix ____ and considering the –OH group attached to C–1.
cards.back: Cyclic alcohols are named using the prefix cyclo and considering the –OH group attached to C–1.
cards.quote: Cyclic alcohols are named using the prefix cyclo and considering the –OH group attached to C–1.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the simplest hydroxy derivative of benzene, and is its common name also an IUPAC name?
cards.back: phenol. It is its common name and also an accepted IUPAC name.
cards.quote: The simplest hydroxy derivative of benzene is phenol. It is its common name and also an accepted IUPAC name.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In the common names of substituted phenols, what do ortho, meta and para denote?
cards.back: the terms ortho (1,2- disubstituted), meta (1,3-disubstituted) and para (1,4-disubstituted) are often used in the common names.
cards.quote: the terms ortho (1,2- disubstituted), meta (1,3-disubstituted) and para (1,4-disubstituted) are often used in the common names.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of o-cresol?
cards.back: 2-Methylphenol
cards.quote: o-Cresol 2-Methylphenol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of m-cresol?
cards.back: 3-Methylphenol
cards.quote: m-Cresol 3-Methylphenol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of p-cresol?
cards.back: 4-Methylphenol
cards.quote: p-Cresol 4-Methylphenol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of catechol?
cards.back: Benzene-1,2-diol
cards.quote: Catechol Benzene-1,2-diol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of resorcinol?
cards.back: Benzene-1,3-diol
cards.quote: Resorcinol Benzene-1,3-diol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of hydroquinone (quinol)?
cards.back: Benzene-1,4-diol
cards.quote: Hydroquinone or quinol Benzene-1,4-diol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are the common names of ethers derived?
cards.back: Common names of ethers are derived from the names of alkyl/aryl groups written as separate words in alphabetical order and adding the word ‘ether’ at the end. For example, CH3OC2H5 is ethylmethyl ether.
cards.quote: Common names of ethers are derived from the names of alkyl/aryl groups written as separate words in alphabetical order and adding the word ‘ether’ at the end. For example, CH3OC2H5 is ethylmethyl ether.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: If both the alkyl groups are the same, the prefix ____ is added before the alkyl group. For example, C2H5OC2H5 is diethyl ether.
cards.back: If both the alkyl groups are the same, the prefix ‘di’ is added before the alkyl group. For example, C2H5OC2H5 is diethyl ether.
cards.quote: If both the alkyl groups are the same, the prefix ‘di’ is added before the alkyl group. For example, C2H5OC2H5 is diethyl ether.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are ethers named in the IUPAC system?
cards.back: According to IUPAC system of nomenclature, ethers are regarded as hydrocarbon derivatives in which a hydrogen atom is replaced by an –OR or –OAr group, where R and Ar represent alkyl and aryl groups, respectively. The larger (R) group is chosen as the parent hydrocarbon.
cards.quote: According to IUPAC system of nomenclature, ethers are regarded as hydrocarbon derivatives in which a hydrogen atom is replaced by an –OR or –OAr group, where R and Ar represent alkyl and aryl groups, respectively. The larger (R) group is chosen as the parent hydrocarbon.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.2: IUPAC name of methyl phenyl ether (anisole)?
cards.back: Methoxybenzene (Anisole)
cards.quote: Methoxybenzene (Anisole)

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 7.2: ethyl phenyl ether is also known as?
cards.back: phenetole
cards.quote: Ethyl phenyl ether (Phenetole)
cards.note: Anisole is methyl phenyl ether; phenetole is ethyl phenyl ether.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The bond angle in alcohols is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (109°-28′). It is due to the ____.
cards.back: The bond angle in alcohols is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (109°-28′). It is due to the repulsion between the unshared electron pairs of oxygen.
cards.quote: The bond angle in alcohols is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (109°-28′). It is due to the repulsion between the unshared electron pairs of oxygen.
blanks: repulsion between the unshared electron pairs of oxygen

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the carbon–oxygen bond length in phenol, compared with methanol?
cards.back: The carbon–oxygen bond length (136 pm) in phenol is slightly less than that in methanol.
cards.quote: The carbon–oxygen bond length (136 pm) in phenol is slightly less than that in methanol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Two reasons why the C–O bond in phenol is shorter than in methanol?
cards.back:
partial double bond character on account of the conjugation of unshared electron pair of oxygen with the aromatic ring
sp2 hybridised state of carbon to which oxygen is attached
cards.quote: This is due to (i) partial double bond character on account of the conjugation of unshared electron pair of oxygen with the aromatic ring (Section 7.4.4) and (ii) sp2 hybridised state of carbon to which oxygen is attached.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In ethers, the four electron pairs, i.e., the two bond pairs and two lone pairs of electrons on oxygen are arranged approximately in a ____.
cards.back: In ethers, the four electron pairs, i.e., the two bond pairs and two lone pairs of electrons on oxygen are arranged approximately in a tetrahedral arrangement.
cards.quote: In ethers, the four electron pairs, i.e., the two bond pairs and two lone pairs of electrons on oxygen are arranged approximately in a tetrahedral arrangement.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are alcohols prepared from alkenes by acid catalysed hydration?
cards.back: Alkenes react with water in the presence of acid as catalyst to form alcohols. In case of unsymmetrical alkenes, the addition reaction takes place in accordance with Markovnikov’s rule.
cards.quote: Alkenes react with water in the presence of acid as catalyst to form alcohols. In case of unsymmetrical alkenes, the addition reaction takes place in accordance with Markovnikov’s rule.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Steps in the mechanism of acid catalysed hydration of an alkene, in order
cards.back:
Step 1: Protonation of alkene to form carbocation by electrophilic attack of H3O+.
Step 2: Nucleophilic attack of water on carbocation.
Step 3: Deprotonation to form an alcohol.
cards.quote: Step 1: Protonation of alkene to form carbocation by electrophilic attack of H3O+. H2O + H+ → H3O+ Step 2: Nucleophilic attack of water on carbocation. Step 3: Deprotonation to form an alcohol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the hydroboration–oxidation reaction of alkenes?
cards.back: Diborane (BH3)2 reacts with alkenes to give trialkyl boranes as addition product. This is oxidised to alcohol by hydrogen peroxide in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide.
cards.quote: Diborane (BH3)2 reacts with alkenes to give trialkyl boranes as addition product. This is oxidised to alcohol by hydrogen peroxide in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The addition of borane to the double bond takes place in such a manner that the boron atom gets attached to the sp2 carbon carrying ____.
cards.back: The addition of borane to the double bond takes place in such a manner that the boron atom gets attached to the sp2 carbon carrying greater number of hydrogen atoms.
cards.quote: The addition of borane to the double bond takes place in such a manner that the boron atom gets attached to the sp2 carbon carrying greater number of hydrogen atoms.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are aldehydes and ketones converted to the corresponding alcohols by hydrogen?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones are reduced to the corresponding alcohols by addition of hydrogen in the presence of catalysts (catalytic hydrogenation).
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones are reduced to the corresponding alcohols by addition of hydrogen in the presence of catalysts (catalytic hydrogenation).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The usual catalyst is a finely divided metal such as ____.
cards.back: The usual catalyst is a finely divided metal such as platinum, palladium or nickel.
cards.quote: The usual catalyst is a finely divided metal such as platinum, palladium or nickel.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Besides catalytic hydrogenation, which two reagents reduce aldehydes and ketones to alcohols?
cards.back:
sodium borohydride (NaBH4)
lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4)
cards.quote: It is also prepared by treating aldehydes and ketones with sodium borohydride (NaBH4) or lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aldehydes yield ____ alcohols whereas ketones give ____ alcohols.
cards.back: Aldehydes yield primary alcohols whereas ketones give secondary alcohols.
cards.quote: Aldehydes yield primary alcohols whereas ketones give secondary alcohols.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols in excellent yields by ____, a strong reducing agent.
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols in excellent yields by lithium aluminium hydride, a strong reducing agent.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols in excellent yields by lithium aluminium hydride, a strong reducing agent.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are carboxylic acids reduced to alcohols commercially?
cards.back: Commercially, acids are reduced to alcohols by converting them to the esters (Section 7.4.4), followed by their reduction using hydrogen in the presence of catalyst (catalytic hydrogenation).
cards.quote: Commercially, acids are reduced to alcohols by converting them to the esters (Section 7.4.4), followed by their reduction using hydrogen in the presence of catalyst (catalytic hydrogenation).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alcohols are produced by the reaction of ____ (Unit 6, Class XII) with aldehydes and ketones.
cards.back: Alcohols are produced by the reaction of Grignard reagents (Unit 6, Class XII) with aldehydes and ketones.
cards.quote: Alcohols are produced by the reaction of Grignard reagents (Unit 6, Class XII) with aldehydes and ketones.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The first step of the reaction is the ____ of Grignard reagent to the carbonyl group to form an adduct. Hydrolysis of the adduct yields an alcohol.
cards.back: The first step of the reaction is the nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagent to the carbonyl group to form an adduct. Hydrolysis of the adduct yields an alcohol.
cards.quote: The first step of the reaction is the nucleophilic addition of Grignard reagent to the carbonyl group to form an adduct. Hydrolysis of the adduct yields an alcohol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The reaction of Grignard reagents with methanal produces a ____, with other aldehydes, ____ and with ketones, ____.
cards.back: The reaction of Grignard reagents with methanal produces a primary alcohol, with other aldehydes, secondary alcohols and with ketones, tertiary alcohols.
cards.quote: The reaction of Grignard reagents with methanal produces a primary alcohol, with other aldehydes, secondary alcohols and with ketones, tertiary alcohols.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Phenol, also known as ____, was first isolated in the early nineteenth century from ____.
cards.back: Phenol, also known as carbolic acid, was first isolated in the early nineteenth century from coal tar.
cards.quote: Phenol, also known as carbolic acid, was first isolated in the early nineteenth century from coal tar.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at ____ and ____. Phenol is obtained by acidification of sodium phenoxide so produced (Unit 6, Class XII).
cards.back: Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623K and 320 atmospheric pressure. Phenol is obtained by acidification of sodium phenoxide so produced (Unit 6, Class XII).
cards.quote: Chlorobenzene is fused with NaOH at 623K and 320 atmospheric pressure. Phenol is obtained by acidification of sodium phenoxide so produced (Unit 6, Class XII).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Steps in preparing phenol from benzene through benzenesulphonic acid, in order
cards.back:
Benzene is sulphonated with oleum
benzene sulphonic acid so formed is converted to sodium phenoxide on heating with molten sodium hydroxide
Acidification of the sodium salt gives phenol.
cards.quote: Benzene is sulphonated with oleum and benzene sulphonic acid so formed is converted to sodium phenoxide on heating with molten sodium hydroxide. Acidification of the sodium salt gives phenol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A diazonium salt is formed by treating an aromatic primary amine with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) at ____.
cards.back: A diazonium salt is formed by treating an aromatic primary amine with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) at 273-278 K.
cards.quote: A diazonium salt is formed by treating an aromatic primary amine with nitrous acid (NaNO2 + HCl) at 273-278 K.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Diazonium salts are hydrolysed to phenols by ____ or by treating with dilute acids
cards.back: Diazonium salts are hydrolysed to phenols by warming with water or by treating with dilute acids
cards.quote: Diazonium salts are hydrolysed to phenols by warming with water or by treating with dilute acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Most of the worldwide production of phenol is from ____.
cards.back: Most of the worldwide production of phenol is from cumene.
cards.quote: Most of the worldwide production of phenol is from cumene.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Steps in the manufacture of phenol from cumene, in order
cards.back:
Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised in the presence of air to cumene hydroperoxide.
It is converted to phenol and acetone by treating it with dilute acid.
cards.quote: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised in the presence of air to cumene hydroperoxide. It is converted to phenol and acetone by treating it with dilute acid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The properties of alcohols and phenols are chiefly due to the ____.
cards.back: The properties of alcohols and phenols are chiefly due to the hydroxyl group.
cards.quote: The properties of alcohols and phenols are chiefly due to the hydroxyl group.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with ____ (increase in van der Waals forces).
cards.back: The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of carbon atoms (increase in van der Waals forces).
cards.quote: The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of carbon atoms (increase in van der Waals forces).
blanks: increase in the number of carbon atoms

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In alcohols, the boiling points ____ in carbon chain (because of decrease in van der Waals forces with decrease in surface area).
cards.back: In alcohols, the boiling points decrease with increase of branching in carbon chain (because of decrease in van der Waals forces with decrease in surface area).
cards.quote: In alcohols, the boiling points decrease with increase of branching in carbon chain (because of decrease in van der Waals forces with decrease in surface area).

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The –OH group in alcohols and phenols is involved in ____
cards.back: The –OH group in alcohols and phenols is involved in intermolecular hydrogen bonding
cards.quote: The –OH group in alcohols and phenols is involved in intermolecular hydrogen bonding

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The high boiling points of alcohols are mainly due to the presence of ____ in them which is lacking in ethers and hydrocarbons.
cards.back: The high boiling points of alcohols are mainly due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding in them which is lacking in ethers and hydrocarbons.
cards.quote: The high boiling points of alcohols are mainly due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding in them which is lacking in ethers and hydrocarbons.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Solubility of alcohols and phenols in water is due to their ability to form ____ with water molecules
cards.back: Solubility of alcohols and phenols in water is due to their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules
cards.quote: Solubility of alcohols and phenols in water is due to their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The solubility ____ with increase in size of alkyl/aryl (hydrophobic) groups.
cards.back: The solubility decreases with increase in size of alkyl/aryl (hydrophobic) groups.
cards.quote: The solubility decreases with increase in size of alkyl/aryl (hydrophobic) groups.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Several of the lower molecular mass alcohols are ____ with water in all proportions.
cards.back: Several of the lower molecular mass alcohols are miscible with water in all proportions.
cards.quote: Several of the lower molecular mass alcohols are miscible with water in all proportions.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Arrange in increasing boiling point: pentan-1-ol, butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, methanol.
cards.back: Methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, butan-1-ol, pentan-1-ol.
cards.quote: Methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, butan-1-ol, pentan-1-ol.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Arrange in increasing boiling point: pentan-1-ol, n-butane, pentanal, ethoxyethane.
cards.back: n-Butane, ethoxyethane, pentanal and pentan-1-ol.
cards.quote: n-Butane, ethoxyethane, pentanal and pentan-1-ol.

source.section: Physical Properties of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The bond between O–H is broken when alcohols react as ____.
cards.back: The bond between O–H is broken when alcohols react as nucleophiles.
cards.quote: The bond between O–H is broken when alcohols react as nucleophiles.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The reactions involving cleavage of C–O bond take place only in alcohols. Phenols show this type of reaction ____.
cards.back: The reactions involving cleavage of C–O bond take place only in alcohols. Phenols show this type of reaction only with zinc.
cards.quote: The reactions involving cleavage of C–O bond take place only in alcohols. Phenols show this type of reaction only with zinc.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alcohols and phenols react with active metals such as ____ to yield corresponding alkoxides/phenoxides and hydrogen.
cards.back: Alcohols and phenols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium and aluminium to yield corresponding alkoxides/phenoxides and hydrogen.
cards.quote: Alcohols and phenols react with active metals such as sodium, potassium and aluminium to yield corresponding alkoxides/phenoxides and hydrogen.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In addition to this, phenols react with ____ to form sodium phenoxides.
cards.back: In addition to this, phenols react with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium phenoxides.
cards.quote: In addition to this, phenols react with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form sodium phenoxides.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The acidic character of alcohols is due to the ____ of O–H bond.
cards.back: The acidic character of alcohols is due to the polar nature of O–H bond.
cards.quote: The acidic character of alcohols is due to the polar nature of O–H bond.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: An electron-releasing group (–CH3, –C2H5) increases electron density on oxygen tending to ____ of O-H bond. This decreases the acid strength.
cards.back: An electron-releasing group (–CH3, –C2H5) increases electron density on oxygen tending to decrease the polarity of O-H bond. This decreases the acid strength.
cards.quote: An electron-releasing group (–CH3, –C2H5) increases electron density on oxygen tending to decrease the polarity of O-H bond. This decreases the acid strength.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alcohols act as Bronsted bases as well. It is due to the presence of unshared electron pairs on oxygen, which makes them ____.
cards.back: Alcohols act as Bronsted bases as well. It is due to the presence of unshared electron pairs on oxygen, which makes them proton acceptors.
cards.quote: Alcohols act as Bronsted bases as well. It is due to the presence of unshared electron pairs on oxygen, which makes them proton acceptors.

source.section: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Phenols

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The reaction of phenol with aqueous sodium hydroxide indicates that phenols are ____.
cards.back: The reaction of phenol with aqueous sodium hydroxide indicates that phenols are stronger acids than alcohols and water.
cards.quote: The reaction of phenol with aqueous sodium hydroxide indicates that phenols are stronger acids than alcohols and water.
blanks: stronger acids than alcohols and water

cards.front: Alkyl aryl ethers are cleaved at the ____ due to the more stable aryl-oxygen bond. The reaction yields phenol and alkyl halide.
cards.back: Alkyl aryl ethers are cleaved at the alkyl-oxygen bond due to the more stable aryl-oxygen bond. The reaction yields phenol and alkyl halide.
cards.quote: Alkyl aryl ethers are cleaved at the alkyl-oxygen bond due to the more stable aryl-oxygen bond. The reaction yields phenol and alkyl halide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Order of reactivity of hydrogen halides in cleaving ethers?
cards.back: HI > HBr > HCl
cards.quote: The order of reactivity of hydrogen halides is as follows: HI > HBr > HCl.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The cleavage of ethers takes place with ____ at high temperature.
cards.back: The cleavage of ethers takes place with concentrated HI or HBr at high temperature.
cards.quote: The cleavage of ethers takes place with concentrated HI or HBr at high temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The reaction of an ether with concentrated HI starts with ____ of ether molecule.
cards.back: The reaction of an ether with concentrated HI starts with protonation of ether molecule.
cards.quote: The reaction of an ether with concentrated HI starts with protonation of ether molecule.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Iodide is a good nucleophile. It attacks the ____ of the oxonium ion formed in step 1 and displaces an alcohol molecule by SN2 mechanism.
cards.back: Iodide is a good nucleophile. It attacks the least substituted carbon of the oxonium ion formed in step 1 and displaces an alcohol molecule by SN2 mechanism.
cards.quote: Iodide is a good nucleophile. It attacks the least substituted carbon of the oxonium ion formed in step 1 and displaces an alcohol molecule by SN2 mechanism.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When primary or secondary alkyl groups are present, it is the ____ that forms alkyl iodide (SN2 reaction).
cards.back: When primary or secondary alkyl groups are present, it is the lower alkyl group that forms alkyl iodide (SN2 reaction).
cards.quote: When primary or secondary alkyl groups are present, it is the lower alkyl group that forms alkyl iodide (SN2 reaction).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The alkoxy group (–OR) is ____ and activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution in the same way as in phenol.
cards.back: The alkoxy group (–OR) is ortho, para directing and activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution in the same way as in phenol.
cards.quote: The alkoxy group (–OR) is ortho, para directing and activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution in the same way as in phenol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts reaction, i.e., the alkyl and acyl groups are introduced at ____
cards.back: Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts reaction, i.e., the alkyl and acyl groups are introduced at ortho and para positions
cards.quote: Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts reaction, i.e., the alkyl and acyl groups are introduced at ortho and para positions

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Anisole reacts with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric and nitric acids to yield a mixture of ____.
cards.back: Anisole reacts with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric and nitric acids to yield a mixture of ortho and para nitroanisole.
cards.quote: Anisole reacts with a mixture of concentrated sulphuric and nitric acids to yield a mixture of ortho and para nitroanisole.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Summary: the bases on which alcohols, phenols and ethers are classified?
cards.back:
on the basis of the number of hydroxyl groups
according to the hybridisation of the carbon atom, sp3 or sp2 to which the –OH group is attached
Ethers are classified on the basis of groups attached to the oxygen atom
cards.quote: Alcohols and phenols are classified (i) on the basis of the number of hydroxyl groups and (ii) according to the hybridisation of the carbon atom, sp3 or sp2 to which the –OH group is attached. Ethers are classified on the basis of groups attached to the oxygen atom.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Summary: the methods of preparing alcohols?
cards.back:
hydration of alkenes
hydroboration-oxidation reaction
catalytic reduction
the action of Grignard reagents
cards.quote: Alcohols may be prepared (1) by hydration of alkenes (i) in presence of an acid and (ii) by hydroboration-oxidation reaction (2) from carbonyl compounds by (i) catalytic reduction and (ii) the action of Grignard reagents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Summary: the methods of preparing phenols?
cards.back:
halogen atom in haloarenes
sulphonic acid group in aryl sulphonic acids
hydrolysis of diazonium salts
industrially from cumene
cards.quote: Phenols may be prepared by (1) substitution of (i) halogen atom in haloarenes and (ii) sulphonic acid group in aryl sulphonic acids, by –OH group (2) by hydrolysis of diazonium salts and (3) industrially from cumene.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with ____ and carboxylic acids with ____ while secondary alcohols yield ketones.
cards.back: On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidising agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidising agents while secondary alcohols yield ketones.
cards.quote: On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidising agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidising agents while secondary alcohols yield ketones.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Tertiary alcohols are ____ to oxidation.
cards.back: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation.
cards.quote: Tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Electron withdrawing groups in phenol ____ its acidic strength and electron releasing groups decrease it.
cards.back: Electron withdrawing groups in phenol increase its acidic strength and electron releasing groups decrease it.
cards.quote: Electron withdrawing groups in phenol increase its acidic strength and electron releasing groups decrease it.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Summary: the methods of preparing ethers?
cards.back:
dehydration of alcohols
Williamson synthesis
cards.quote: Ethers may be prepared by (i) dehydration of alcohols and (ii) Williamson synthesis.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the carbonyl group?
cards.back: carbon-oxygen double bond (>C=O) called carbonyl group, which is one of the most important functional groups in organic chemistry.
cards.quote: the organic compounds containing carbon-oxygen double bond (>C=O) called carbonyl group, which is one of the most important functional groups in organic chemistry.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aldehydes vs ketones: the difference on the atoms bonded to the carbonyl group.
cards.back: In aldehydes, the carbonyl group is bonded to a carbon and hydrogen while in the ketones, it is bonded to two carbon atoms.
cards.quote: In aldehydes, the carbonyl group is bonded to a carbon and hydrogen while in the ketones, it is bonded to two carbon atoms.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which carbonyl compounds are called carboxylic acids, amides and acyl halides?
cards.back: The carbonyl compounds in which carbon of carbonyl group is bonded to carbon or hydrogen and oxygen of hydroxyl moiety (-OH) are known as carboxylic acids, while in compounds where carbon is attached to carbon or hydrogen and nitrogen of -NH2 moiety or to halogens are called amides and acyl halides respectively.
cards.quote: The carbonyl compounds in which carbon of carbonyl group is bonded to carbon or hydrogen and oxygen of hydroxyl moiety (-OH) are known as carboxylic acids, while in compounds where carbon is attached to carbon or hydrogen and nitrogen of -NH2 moiety or to halogens are called amides and acyl halides respectively.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which compounds are derivatives of carboxylic acids?
cards.back: Esters and anhydrides are derivatives of carboxylic acids.
cards.quote: Esters and anhydrides are derivatives of carboxylic acids.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are the common names of most aldehydes derived?
cards.back: The common names of most aldehydes are derived from the common names of the corresponding carboxylic acids [Section 8.6.1] by replacing the ending –ic of acid with aldehyde.
cards.quote: The common names of most aldehydes are derived from the common names of the corresponding carboxylic acids [Section 8.6.1] by replacing the ending –ic of acid with aldehyde.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are the common names of ketones derived?
cards.back: The common names of ketones are derived by naming two alkyl or aryl groups bonded to the carbonyl group.
cards.quote: The common names of ketones are derived by naming two alkyl or aryl groups bonded to the carbonyl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Some ketones have historical common names, the simplest dimethyl ketone is called ____.
cards.back: Some ketones have historical common names, the simplest dimethyl ketone is called acetone.
cards.quote: Some ketones have historical common names, the simplest dimethyl ketone is called acetone.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alkyl phenyl ketones are usually named by adding the name of acyl group as prefix to the word ____.
cards.back: Alkyl phenyl ketones are usually named by adding the name of acyl group as prefix to the word phenone.
cards.quote: Alkyl phenyl ketones are usually named by adding the name of acyl group as prefix to the word phenone.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are IUPAC names of open chain aliphatic aldehydes and ketones derived from alkanes?
cards.back: The IUPAC names of open chain aliphatic aldehydes and ketones are derived from the names of the corresponding alkanes by replacing the ending –e with –al and –one respectively.
cards.quote: The IUPAC names of open chain aliphatic aldehydes and ketones are derived from the names of the corresponding alkanes by replacing the ending –e with –al and –one respectively.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aldehydes vs ketones: the difference on how the carbon chain is numbered in IUPAC names.
cards.back: In case of aldehydes the longest carbon chain is numbered starting from the carbon of the aldehyde group while in case of ketones the numbering begins from the end nearer to the carbonyl group.
cards.quote: In case of aldehydes the longest carbon chain is numbered starting from the carbon of the aldehyde group while in case of ketones the numbering begins from the end nearer to the carbonyl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When the aldehyde group is attached to a ring, the suffix ____ is added after the full name of the cycloalkane.
cards.back: When the aldehyde group is attached to a ring, the suffix carbaldehyde is added after the full name of the cycloalkane.
cards.quote: When the aldehyde group is attached to a ring, the suffix carbaldehyde is added after the full name of the cycloalkane.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the IUPAC name of the simplest aromatic aldehyde, and is benzaldehyde accepted?
cards.back: The name of the simplest aromatic aldehyde carrying the aldehyde group on a benzene ring is benzenecarbaldehyde. However, the common name benzaldehyde is also accepted by IUPAC.
cards.quote: The name of the simplest aromatic aldehyde carrying the aldehyde group on a benzene ring is benzenecarbaldehyde. However, the common name benzaldehyde is also accepted by IUPAC.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: common names of HCHO, CH3CHO and (CH3)2CHCHO, in order.
cards.back:
Formaldehyde
Acetaldehyde
Isobutyraldehyde
cards.quote: Formaldehyde Acetaldehyde Isobutyraldehyde

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: IUPAC names of HCHO, CH3CHO and (CH3)2CHCHO, in order.
cards.back:
Methanal
Ethanal
2-Methylpropanal
cards.quote: Methanal Ethanal 2-Methylpropanal

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: IUPAC names of CH3CH(OCH3)CHO, CH3CH2CH2CH2CHO and CH2=CHCHO, in order.
cards.back:
2-Methoxypropanal
Pentanal
Prop-2-enal
cards.quote: 2-Methoxypropanal Pentanal Prop-2-enal

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: common names of CH3COCH2CH2CH3 and (CH3)2CHCOCH(CH3)2, in order.
cards.back:
Methyl n-propyl ketone
Diisopropyl ketone
cards.quote: Methyl n-propyl ketone Diisopropyl ketone

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: IUPAC names of CH3COCH2CH2CH3 and (CH3)2CHCOCH(CH3)2, in order.
cards.back:
Pentan-2-one
2,4-Dimethylpentan-3-one
cards.quote: Pentan-2-one 2,4-Dimethylpentan-3-one

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.1: IUPAC name of the ketone (CH3)2C=CHCOCH3, whose common name is mesityl oxide.
cards.back: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one
cards.quote: 4-Methylpent-3-en-2-one

source.section: Table 8.1: Common and IUPAC Names of Some Aldehydes and Ketones

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the bond angles in the carbonyl group, and which structure do they suit?
cards.back: The bond angles are approximately 120° as expected of a trigonal coplanar structure (Figure 8.1).
cards.quote: The bond angles are approximately 120° as expected of a trigonal coplanar structure (Figure 8.1).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is the carbon-oxygen double bond of the carbonyl group polarised?
cards.back: The carbon-oxygen double bond is polarised due to higher electronegativity of oxygen relative to carbon.
cards.quote: The carbon-oxygen double bond is polarised due to higher electronegativity of oxygen relative to carbon.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: On what basis is the high polarity of the carbonyl group explained?
cards.back: The high polarity of the carbonyl group is explained on the basis of resonance involving a neutral (A) and a dipolar (B) structures as shown.
cards.quote: The high polarity of the carbonyl group is explained on the basis of resonance involving a neutral (A) and a dipolar (B) structures as shown.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are aldehydes and ketones generally prepared from alcohols by oxidation?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones are generally prepared by oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols, respectively (Unit 7, Class XII).
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones are generally prepared by oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols, respectively (Unit 7, Class XII).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Dehydrogenation of alcohols: for which alcohols is it suitable, and which catalysts are used?
cards.back: This method is suitable for volatile alcohols and is of industrial application. In this method alcohol vapours are passed over heavy metal catalysts (Ag or Cu).
cards.quote: This method is suitable for volatile alcohols and is of industrial application. In this method alcohol vapours are passed over heavy metal catalysts (Ag or Cu).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does ozonolysis of alkenes followed by zinc dust and water give?
cards.back: ozonolysis of alkenes followed by reaction with zinc dust and water gives aldehydes, ketones or a mixture of both depending on the substitution pattern of the alkene
cards.quote: ozonolysis of alkenes followed by reaction with zinc dust and water gives aldehydes, ketones or a mixture of both depending on the substitution pattern of the alkene

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do all alkynes other than ethyne give on hydration with H2SO4 and HgSO4?
cards.back: All other alkynes give ketones in this reaction (Unit 9, Class XI).
cards.quote: All other alkynes give ketones in this reaction (Unit 9, Class XI).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which acyl chloride is hydrogenated over palladium on barium sulphate to give an aldehyde.
cards.back: Acyl chloride (acid chloride) is hydrogenated over catalyst, palladium on barium sulphate. This reaction is called Rosenmund reduction.
cards.quote: Acyl chloride (acid chloride) is hydrogenated over catalyst, palladium on barium sulphate. This reaction is called Rosenmund reduction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which nitriles are reduced by stannous chloride and HCl to an imine, then hydrolysed to an aldehyde.
cards.back: Nitriles are reduced to corresponding imine with stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid, which on hydrolysis give corresponding aldehyde. This reaction is called Stephen reaction.
cards.quote: Nitriles are reduced to corresponding imine with stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid, which on hydrolysis give corresponding aldehyde. This reaction is called Stephen reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which reagent reduces esters to aldehydes?
cards.back: esters are also reduced to aldehydes with DIBAL-H.
cards.quote: esters are also reduced to aldehydes with DIBAL-H.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which chromyl chloride oxidises the methyl group of toluene to a chromium complex that hydrolyses to benzaldehyde.
cards.back: Chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding benzaldehyde. This reaction is called Etard reaction.
cards.quote: Chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding benzaldehyde. This reaction is called Etard reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How does chromic oxide in acetic anhydride convert toluene into benzaldehyde?
cards.back: Toluene or substituted toluene is converted to benzylidene diacetate on treating with chromic oxide in acetic anhydride. The benzylidene diacetate can be hydrolysed to corresponding benzaldehyde with aqueous acid.
cards.quote: Toluene or substituted toluene is converted to benzylidene diacetate on treating with chromic oxide in acetic anhydride. The benzylidene diacetate can be hydrolysed to corresponding benzaldehyde with aqueous acid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the commercial method of manufacture of benzaldehyde from toluene?
cards.back: Side chain chlorination of toluene gives benzal chloride, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde. This is a commercial method of manufacture of benzaldehyde.
cards.quote: Side chain chlorination of toluene gives benzal chloride, which on hydrolysis gives benzaldehyde. This is a commercial method of manufacture of benzaldehyde.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which benzene treated with CO and HCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 or CuCl gives benzaldehyde.
cards.back: When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride or cuprous chloride, it gives benzaldehyde or substituted benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as Gatterman-Koch reaction.
cards.quote: When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride or cuprous chloride, it gives benzaldehyde or substituted benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as Gatterman-Koch reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are ketones prepared from acyl chlorides and dialkylcadmium?
cards.back: Treatment of acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium, prepared by the reaction of cadmium chloride with Grignard reagent, gives ketones.
cards.quote: Treatment of acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium, prepared by the reaction of cadmium chloride with Grignard reagent, gives ketones.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Treating a nitrile with Grignard reagent followed by hydrolysis yields a ____.
cards.back: Treating a nitrile with Grignard reagent followed by hydrolysis yields a ketone.
cards.quote: Treating a nitrile with Grignard reagent followed by hydrolysis yields a ketone.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which benzene treated with acid chloride and anhydrous AlCl3 gives a ketone.
cards.back: When benzene or substituted benzene is treated with acid chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride, it affords the corresponding ketone. This reaction is known as Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction.
cards.quote: When benzene or substituted benzene is treated with acid chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride, it affords the corresponding ketone. This reaction is known as Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the physical state of methanal, ethanal and other aldehydes and ketones at room temperature?
cards.back: Methanal is a gas at room temperature. Ethanal is a volatile liquid. Other aldehydes and ketones are liquid or solid at room temperature.
cards.quote: Methanal is a gas at room temperature. Ethanal is a volatile liquid. Other aldehydes and ketones are liquid or solid at room temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do boiling points of aldehydes and ketones compare with hydrocarbons and ethers of comparable molecular masses, and why?
cards.back: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons and ethers of comparable molecular masses. It is due to weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones arising out of the dipole-dipole interactions.
cards.quote: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons and ethers of comparable molecular masses. It is due to weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones arising out of the dipole-dipole interactions.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are boiling points of aldehydes and ketones lower than those of alcohols of similar molecular masses?
cards.back: Also, their boiling points are lower than those of alcohols of similar molecular masses due to absence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
cards.quote: Also, their boiling points are lower than those of alcohols of similar molecular masses due to absence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Arrange in increasing order of boiling point (molecular masses 58 and 60): propan-1-ol, n-butane, acetone, methoxyethane, propanal.
cards.back:
n-Butane
Methoxyethane
Propanal
Acetone
Propan-1-ol
cards.quote: n-Butane Methoxyethane Propanal Acetone Propan-1-ol

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which lower aldehydes and ketones are miscible with water in all proportions, and why?
cards.back: The lower members of aldehydes and ketones such as methanal, ethanal and propanone are miscible with water in all proportions, because they form hydrogen bond with water.
cards.quote: The lower members of aldehydes and ketones such as methanal, ethanal and propanone are miscible with water in all proportions, because they form hydrogen bond with water.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How does the solubility of aldehydes and ketones in water change with the length of the alkyl chain?
cards.back: the solubility of aldehydes and ketones decreases rapidly on increasing the length of alkyl chain.
cards.quote: the solubility of aldehydes and ketones decreases rapidly on increasing the length of alkyl chain.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do the odours of aldehydes change as the size of the molecule increases?
cards.back: The lower aldehydes have sharp pungent odours. As the size of the molecule increases, the odour becomes less pungent and more fragrant.
cards.quote: The lower aldehydes have sharp pungent odours. As the size of the molecule increases, the odour becomes less pungent and more fragrant.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Do aldehydes and ketones undergo electrophilic or nucleophilic addition reactions?
cards.back: Contrary to electrophilic addition reactions observed in alkenes, the aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions.
cards.quote: Contrary to electrophilic addition reactions observed in alkenes, the aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition reactions.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group, which atom does the nucleophile attack and from which direction?
cards.back: A nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon atom of the polar carbonyl group from a direction approximately perpendicular to the plane of sp2 hybridised orbitals of carbonyl carbon (Fig. 8.2).
cards.quote: A nucleophile attacks the electrophilic carbon atom of the polar carbonyl group from a direction approximately perpendicular to the plane of sp2 hybridised orbitals of carbonyl carbon (Fig. 8.2).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In nucleophilic addition, how does the hybridisation of carbonyl carbon change and what intermediate is produced?
cards.back: The hybridisation of carbon changes from sp2 to sp3 in this process, and a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate is produced.
cards.quote: The hybridisation of carbon changes from sp2 to sp3 in this process, and a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate is produced.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which are more reactive in nucleophilic addition reactions, aldehydes or ketones?
cards.back: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons.
cards.quote: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why do ketones hinder the approach of a nucleophile more than aldehydes (steric reason)?
cards.back: Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of nucleophile to carbonyl carbon than in aldehydes having only one such substituent.
cards.quote: Sterically, the presence of two relatively large substituents in ketones hinders the approach of nucleophile to carbonyl carbon than in aldehydes having only one such substituent.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are aldehydes more reactive than ketones electronically?
cards.back: Electronically, aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more effectively than in former.
cards.quote: Electronically, aldehydes are more reactive than ketones because two alkyl groups reduce the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon more effectively than in former.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Is benzaldehyde more or less reactive than propanal in nucleophilic addition, and why?
cards.back: The carbon atom of the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde is less electrophilic than carbon atom of the carbonyl group present in propanal. The polarity of the carbonyl group is reduced in benzaldehyde due to resonance as shown below and hence it is less reactive than propanal.
cards.quote: The carbon atom of the carbonyl group of benzaldehyde is less electrophilic than carbon atom of the carbonyl group present in propanal. The polarity of the carbonyl group is reduced in benzaldehyde due to resonance as shown below and hence it is less reactive than propanal.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do aldehydes and ketones yield with hydrogen cyanide (HCN)?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones react with hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to yield cyanohydrins.
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones react with hydrogen cyanide (HCN) to yield cyanohydrins.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is the addition of HCN to carbonyl compounds catalysed by a base?
cards.back: This reaction occurs very slowly with pure HCN. Therefore, it is catalysed by a base and the generated cyanide ion (CN-) being a stronger nucleophile readily adds to carbonyl compounds to yield corresponding cyanohydrin.
cards.quote: This reaction occurs very slowly with pure HCN. Therefore, it is catalysed by a base and the generated cyanide ion (CN-) being a stronger nucleophile readily adds to carbonyl compounds to yield corresponding cyanohydrin.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Sodium hydrogensulphite addition: aldehydes vs ketones, the difference on the position of equilibrium.
cards.back: The position of the equilibrium lies largely to the right hand side for most aldehydes and to the left for most ketones due to steric reasons.
cards.quote: The position of the equilibrium lies largely to the right hand side for most aldehydes and to the left for most ketones due to steric reasons.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is the hydrogensulphite addition compound of aldehydes useful?
cards.back: The hydrogensulphite addition compound is water soluble and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali. Therefore, these are useful for separation and purification of aldehydes.
cards.quote: The hydrogensulphite addition compound is water soluble and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali. Therefore, these are useful for separation and purification of aldehydes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are hemiacetals and acetals (aldehydes with a monohydric alcohol and dry HCl)?
cards.back: Aldehydes react with one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride to yield alkoxyalcohol intermediate, known as hemiacetals, which further react with one more molecule of alcohol to give a gem-dialkoxy compound known as acetal as shown in the reaction.
cards.quote: Aldehydes react with one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride to yield alkoxyalcohol intermediate, known as hemiacetals, which further react with one more molecule of alcohol to give a gem-dialkoxy compound known as acetal as shown in the reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are ethylene glycol ketals?
cards.back: Ketones react with ethylene glycol under similar conditions to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals.
cards.quote: Ketones react with ethylene glycol under similar conditions to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the role of dry hydrogen chloride in acetal and ketal formation?
cards.back: Dry hydrogen chloride protonates the oxygen of the carbonyl compounds and therefore, increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon facilitating the nucleophilic attack of ethylene glycol.
cards.quote: Dry hydrogen chloride protonates the oxygen of the carbonyl compounds and therefore, increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon facilitating the nucleophilic attack of ethylene glycol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do acetals and ketals give on hydrolysis with aqueous mineral acids?
cards.back: Acetals and ketals are hydrolysed with aqueous mineral acids to yield corresponding aldehydes and ketones respectively.
cards.quote: Acetals and ketals are hydrolysed with aqueous mineral acids to yield corresponding aldehydes and ketones respectively.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do ammonia and its derivatives H2N-Z react with aldehydes and ketones, and is the reaction reversible?
cards.back: Nucleophiles, such as ammonia and its derivatives H2N-Z add to the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones. The reaction is reversible and catalysed by acid.
cards.quote: Nucleophiles, such as ammonia and its derivatives H2N-Z add to the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones. The reaction is reversible and catalysed by acid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why does the equilibrium in the addition of H2N-Z to carbonyl compounds favour product formation?
cards.back: The equilibrium favours the product formation due to rapid dehydration of the intermediate to form >C=N-Z.
cards.quote: The equilibrium favours the product formation due to rapid dehydration of the intermediate to form >C=N-Z.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 8.2: carbonyl derivatives formed from hydroxylamine, hydrazine and phenylhydrazine, in order.
cards.back:
Oxime
Hydrazone
Phenylhydrazone
cards.quote: Oxime Hydrazone Phenylhydrazone

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: 2,4-DNP-derivatives are ____ solids, useful for characterisation of aldehydes and ketones.
cards.back: 2,4-DNP-derivatives are yellow, orange or red solids, useful for characterisation of aldehydes and ketones.
cards.quote: 2,4-DNP-derivatives are yellow, orange or red solids, useful for characterisation of aldehydes and ketones.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do NaBH4, LiAlH4 or catalytic hydrogenation convert aldehydes and ketones into?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones are reduced to primary and secondary alcohols respectively by sodium borohydride (NaBH4) or lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4) as well as by catalytic hydrogenation (Unit 7, Class XII).
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones are reduced to primary and secondary alcohols respectively by sodium borohydride (NaBH4) or lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4) as well as by catalytic hydrogenation (Unit 7, Class XII).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which oxidising agents oxidise aldehydes to carboxylic acids, including the mild ones?
cards.back: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids on treatment with common oxidising agents like nitric acid, potassium permanganate, potassium dichromate, etc. Even mild oxidising agents, mainly Tollens' reagent and Fehlings' reagent also oxidise aldehydes.
cards.quote: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids on treatment with common oxidising agents like nitric acid, potassium permanganate, potassium dichromate, etc. Even mild oxidising agents, mainly Tollens' reagent and Fehlings' reagent also oxidise aldehydes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Under what conditions are ketones oxidised, and what do they give?
cards.back: Ketones are generally oxidised under vigorous conditions, i.e., strong oxidising agents and at elevated temperatures. Their oxidation involves carbon-carbon bond cleavage to afford a mixture of carboxylic acids having lesser number of carbon atoms than the parent ketone.
cards.quote: Ketones are generally oxidised under vigorous conditions, i.e., strong oxidising agents and at elevated temperatures. Their oxidation involves carbon-carbon bond cleavage to afford a mixture of carboxylic acids having lesser number of carbon atoms than the parent ketone.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Tollens' test: what is observed on warming an aldehyde with Tollens' reagent, and in which medium?
cards.back: On warming an aldehyde with freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate solution (Tollens' reagent), a bright silver mirror is produced due to the formation of silver metal. The aldehydes are oxidised to corresponding carboxylate anion. The reaction occurs in alkaline medium.
cards.quote: On warming an aldehyde with freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate solution (Tollens' reagent), a bright silver mirror is produced due to the formation of silver metal. The aldehydes are oxidised to corresponding carboxylate anion. The reaction occurs in alkaline medium.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does Fehling's reagent comprise?
cards.back: Fehling reagent comprises of two solutions, Fehling solution A and Fehling solution B. Fehling solution A is aqueous copper sulphate and Fehling solution B is alkaline sodium potassium tartarate (Rochelle salt). These two solutions are mixed in equal amounts before test.
cards.quote: Fehling reagent comprises of two solutions, Fehling solution A and Fehling solution B. Fehling solution A is aqueous copper sulphate and Fehling solution B is alkaline sodium potassium tartarate (Rochelle salt). These two solutions are mixed in equal amounts before test.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Fehling's test: what is obtained on heating an aldehyde with Fehling's reagent, and which aldehydes do not respond?
cards.back: On heating an aldehyde with Fehling's reagent, a reddish brown precipitate is obtained. Aldehydes are oxidised to corresponding carboxylate anion. Aromatic aldehydes do not respond to this test.
cards.quote: On heating an aldehyde with Fehling's reagent, a reddish brown precipitate is obtained. Aldehydes are oxidised to corresponding carboxylate anion. Aromatic aldehydes do not respond to this test.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What happens to methyl ketones on oxidation with sodium hypohalite (haloform reaction)?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one methyl group linked to the carbonyl carbon atom (methyl ketones) are oxidised by sodium hypohalite to sodium salts of corresponding carboxylic acids having one carbon atom less than that of carbonyl compound. The methyl group is converted to haloform.
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one methyl group linked to the carbonyl carbon atom (methyl ketones) are oxidised by sodium hypohalite to sodium salts of corresponding carboxylic acids having one carbon atom less than that of carbonyl compound. The methyl group is converted to haloform.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the iodoform reaction with sodium hypoiodite used to detect?
cards.back: Iodoform reaction with sodium hypoiodite is also used for detection of CH3CO group or CH3CH(OH) group which produces CH3CO group on oxidation.
cards.quote: Iodoform reaction with sodium hypoiodite is also used for detection of CH3CO group or CH3CH(OH) group which produces CH3CO group on oxidation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are the α-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones acidic?
cards.back: The acidity of α-hydrogen atoms of carbonyl compounds is due to the strong electron withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group and resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base.
cards.quote: The acidity of α-hydrogen atoms of carbonyl compounds is due to the strong electron withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group and resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base.

source.section: 8.4 Chemical Reactions: 4. Reactions due to α-hydrogen

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do aldehydes and ketones having at least one α-hydrogen form with dilute alkali (Aldol reaction)?
cards.back: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one α-hydrogen undergo a reaction in the presence of dilute alkali as catalyst to form β-hydroxy aldehydes (aldol) or β-hydroxy ketones (ketol), respectively. This is known as Aldol reaction.
cards.quote: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one α-hydrogen undergo a reaction in the presence of dilute alkali as catalyst to form β-hydroxy aldehydes (aldol) or β-hydroxy ketones (ketol), respectively. This is known as Aldol reaction.

source.section: 8.4 Chemical Reactions: 4. Reactions due to α-hydrogen

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: From which two functional groups is the name aldol derived?
cards.back: The name aldol is derived from the names of the two functional groups, aldehyde and alcohol, present in the products.
cards.quote: The name aldol is derived from the names of the two functional groups, aldehyde and alcohol, present in the products.

source.section: 8.4 Chemical Reactions: 4. Reactions due to α-hydrogen

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is Aldol condensation?
cards.back: The aldol and ketol readily lose water to give α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds which are aldol condensation products and the reaction is called Aldol condensation.
cards.quote: The aldol and ketol readily lose water to give α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds which are aldol condensation products and the reaction is called Aldol condensation.

source.section: 8.4 Chemical Reactions: 4. Reactions due to α-hydrogen

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do aromatic aldehydes and ketones undergo electrophilic substitution, and what is the role of the carbonyl group?
cards.back: Aromatic aldehydes and ketones undergo electrophilic substitution at the ring in which the carbonyl group acts as a deactivating and meta-directing group.
cards.quote: Aromatic aldehydes and ketones undergo electrophilic substitution at the ring in which the carbonyl group acts as a deactivating and meta-directing group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is formaldehyde well known as, and what is it used for?
cards.back: Formaldehyde is well known as formalin (40%) solution used to preserve biological specimens and to prepare bakelite (a phenol-formaldehyde resin), urea-formaldehyde glues and other polymeric products.
cards.quote: Formaldehyde is well known as formalin (40%) solution used to preserve biological specimens and to prepare bakelite (a phenol-formaldehyde resin), urea-formaldehyde glues and other polymeric products.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is acetaldehyde used for primarily?
cards.back: Acetaldehyde is used primarily as a starting material in the manufacture of acetic acid, ethyl acetate, vinyl acetate, polymers and drugs.
cards.quote: Acetaldehyde is used primarily as a starting material in the manufacture of acetic acid, ethyl acetate, vinyl acetate, polymers and drugs.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Benzaldehyde is used in ____ and in dye industries.
cards.back: Benzaldehyde is used in perfumery and in dye industries.
cards.quote: Benzaldehyde is used in perfumery and in dye industries.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Acetone and ethyl methyl ketone are common industrial ____.
cards.back: Acetone and ethyl methyl ketone are common industrial solvents.
cards.quote: Acetone and ethyl methyl ketone are common industrial solvents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are carboxylic acids?
cards.back: Carbon compounds containing a carboxyl functional group, –COOH are called carboxylic acids.
cards.quote: Carbon compounds containing a carboxyl functional group, –COOH are called carboxylic acids.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is the –COOH group called the carboxyl group?
cards.back: The carboxyl group, consists of a carbonyl group attached to a hydroxyl group, hence its name carboxyl.
cards.quote: The carboxyl group, consists of a carbonyl group attached to a hydroxyl group, hence its name carboxyl.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Types of carboxylic acids by the group attached to the carboxylic carbon.
cards.back:
aliphatic (RCOOH)
aromatic (ArCOOH)
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids may be aliphatic (RCOOH) or aromatic (ArCOOH) depending on the group, alkyl or aryl, attached to carboxylic carbon.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are fatty acids and where do they occur?
cards.back: Some higher members of aliphatic carboxylic acids (C12 – C18) known as fatty acids, occur in natural fats as esters of glycerol.
cards.quote: Some higher members of aliphatic carboxylic acids (C12 – C18) known as fatty acids, occur in natural fats as esters of glycerol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Carboxylic acids serve as starting material for which important organic compounds?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids serve as starting material for several other important organic compounds such as anhydrides, esters, acid chlorides, amides, etc.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids serve as starting material for several other important organic compounds such as anhydrides, esters, acid chlorides, amides, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: From what sources were formic, acetic and butyric acid first obtained?
cards.back: formic acid (HCOOH) was first obtained from red ants (Latin: formica means ant), acetic acid (CH3COOH) from vinegar (Latin: acetum, means vinegar), butyric acid (CH3CH2CH2COOH) from rancid butter (Latin: butyrum, means butter).
cards.quote: formic acid (HCOOH) was first obtained from red ants (Latin: formica means ant), acetic acid (CH3COOH) from vinegar (Latin: acetum, means vinegar), butyric acid (CH3CH2CH2COOH) from rancid butter (Latin: butyrum, means butter).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are common names of carboxylic acids formed and from what are they derived?
cards.back: The common names end with the suffix –ic acid and have been derived from Latin or Greek names of their natural sources.
cards.quote: The common names end with the suffix –ic acid and have been derived from Latin or Greek names of their natural sources.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are aliphatic carboxylic acids named in the IUPAC system, and which carbon is numbered one?
cards.back: In the IUPAC system, aliphatic carboxylic acids are named by replacing the ending –e in the name of the corresponding alkane with – oic acid. In numbering the carbon chain, the carboxylic carbon is numbered one.
cards.quote: In the IUPAC system, aliphatic carboxylic acids are named by replacing the ending –e in the name of the corresponding alkane with – oic acid. In numbering the carbon chain, the carboxylic carbon is numbered one.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are compounds with more than one carboxyl group named in the IUPAC system?
cards.back: For naming compounds containing more than one carboxyl group, the alkyl chain leaving carboxyl groups is numbered and the number of carboxyl groups is indicated by adding the multiplicative prefix, dicarboxylic acid, tricarboxylic acid, etc. to the name of parent alkyl chain.
cards.quote: For naming compounds containing more than one carboxyl group, the alkyl chain leaving carboxyl groups is numbered and the number of carboxyl groups is indicated by adding the multiplicative prefix, dicarboxylic acid, tricarboxylic acid, etc. to the name of parent alkyl chain.

cards.front: Table 8.3: common names of HCOOH, CH3COOH, CH3CH2COOH, CH3CH2CH2COOH and (CH3)2CHCOOH, in order.
cards.back:

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the bond angles at the carboxyl carbon, and are the bonds in one plane?
cards.back: In carboxylic acids, the bonds to the carboxyl carbon lie in one plane and are separated by about 120°.
cards.quote: In carboxylic acids, the bonds to the carboxyl carbon lie in one plane and are separated by about 120°.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which reagents oxidise primary alcohols to carboxylic acids (Jones reagent)?
cards.back: Primary alcohols are readily oxidised to carboxylic acids with common oxidising agents such as potassium permanganate (KMnO4) in neutral, acidic or alkaline media or by potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7) and chromium trioxide (CrO3) in acidic media (Jones reagent).
cards.quote: Primary alcohols are readily oxidised to carboxylic acids with common oxidising agents such as potassium permanganate (KMnO4) in neutral, acidic or alkaline media or by potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7) and chromium trioxide (CrO3) in acidic media (Jones reagent).

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are carboxylic acids prepared from aldehydes?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are also prepared from aldehydes by the use of mild oxidising agents (Section 8.4).
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are also prepared from aldehydes by the use of mild oxidising agents (Section 8.4).

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are aromatic carboxylic acids prepared from alkylbenzenes?
cards.back: Aromatic carboxylic acids can be prepared by vigorous oxidation of alkyl benzenes with chromic acid or acidic or alkaline potassium permanganate. The entire side chain is oxidised to the carboxyl group irrespective of length of the side chain.
cards.quote: Aromatic carboxylic acids can be prepared by vigorous oxidation of alkyl benzenes with chromic acid or acidic or alkaline potassium permanganate. The entire side chain is oxidised to the carboxyl group irrespective of length of the side chain.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary and secondary alkyl groups are oxidised in this manner while ____ group is not affected.
cards.back: Primary and secondary alkyl groups are oxidised in this manner while tertiary group is not affected.
cards.quote: Primary and secondary alkyl groups are oxidised in this manner while tertiary group is not affected.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do nitriles give on hydrolysis, and how is the reaction stopped at the amide stage?
cards.back: Nitriles are hydrolysed to amides and then to acids in the presence of H+ or OH- as catalyst. Mild reaction conditions are used to stop the reaction at the amide stage.
cards.quote: Nitriles are hydrolysed to amides and then to acids in the presence of H+ or OH- as catalyst. Mild reaction conditions are used to stop the reaction at the amide stage.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are carboxylic acids prepared from Grignard reagents and carbon dioxide?
cards.back: Grignard reagents react with carbon dioxide (dry ice) to form salts of carboxylic acids which in turn give corresponding carboxylic acids after acidification with mineral acid.
cards.quote: Grignard reagents react with carbon dioxide (dry ice) to form salts of carboxylic acids which in turn give corresponding carboxylic acids after acidification with mineral acid.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do the nitrile and Grignard methods achieve in converting alkyl halides to carboxylic acids?
