cards.back: The above methods (3 and 4) are useful for converting alkyl halides into corresponding carboxylic acids having one carbon atom more than that present in alkyl halides (ascending the series).
cards.quote: The above methods (3 and 4) are useful for converting alkyl halides into corresponding carboxylic acids having one carbon atom more than that present in alkyl halides (ascending the series).

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are carboxylic acids obtained from acid chlorides and anhydrides?
cards.back: Acid chlorides when hydrolysed with water give carboxylic acids or more readily hydrolysed with aqueous base to give carboxylate ions which on acidification provide corresponding carboxylic acids. Anhydrides on the other hand are hydrolysed to corresponding acid(s) with water.
cards.quote: Acid chlorides when hydrolysed with water give carboxylic acids or more readily hydrolysed with aqueous base to give carboxylate ions which on acidification provide corresponding carboxylic acids. Anhydrides on the other hand are hydrolysed to corresponding acid(s) with water.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does acidic hydrolysis of esters give, and what does basic hydrolysis give?
cards.back: Acidic hydrolysis of esters gives directly carboxylic acids while basic hydrolysis gives carboxylates, which on acidification give corresponding carboxylic acids.
cards.quote: Acidic hydrolysis of esters gives directly carboxylic acids while basic hydrolysis gives carboxylates, which on acidification give corresponding carboxylic acids.

source.section: 8.7 Methods of Preparation of Carboxylic Acids

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the physical state and odour of aliphatic carboxylic acids up to nine carbon atoms?
cards.back: Aliphatic carboxylic acids upto nine carbon atoms are colourless liquids at room temperature with unpleasant odours.
cards.quote: Aliphatic carboxylic acids upto nine carbon atoms are colourless liquids at room temperature with unpleasant odours.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are the higher carboxylic acids practically odourless?
cards.back: The higher acids are wax like solids and are practically odourless due to their low volatility.
cards.quote: The higher acids are wax like solids and are practically odourless due to their low volatility.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why do carboxylic acids boil higher than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are higher boiling liquids than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses. This is due to more extensive association of carboxylic acid molecules through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are higher boiling liquids than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses. This is due to more extensive association of carboxylic acid molecules through intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In what form do most carboxylic acids exist in the vapour phase or in aprotic solvents?
cards.back: most carboxylic acids exist as dimer in the vapour phase or in the aprotic solvents.
cards.quote: most carboxylic acids exist as dimer in the vapour phase or in the aprotic solvents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Up to how many carbon atoms are simple aliphatic carboxylic acids miscible in water?
cards.back: Simple aliphatic carboxylic acids having upto four carbon atoms are miscible in water due to the formation of hydrogen bonds with water. The solubility decreases with increasing number of carbon atoms.
cards.quote: Simple aliphatic carboxylic acids having upto four carbon atoms are miscible in water due to the formation of hydrogen bonds with water. The solubility decreases with increasing number of carbon atoms.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are higher carboxylic acids practically insoluble in water?
cards.back: Higher carboxylic acids are practically insoluble in water due to the increased hydrophobic interaction of hydrocarbon part.
cards.quote: Higher carboxylic acids are practically insoluble in water due to the increased hydrophobic interaction of hydrocarbon part.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How soluble is benzoic acid in cold water, and in which solvents are carboxylic acids soluble?
cards.back: Benzoic acid, the simplest aromatic carboxylic acid is nearly insoluble in cold water. Carboxylic acids are also soluble in less polar organic solvents like benzene, ether, alcohol, chloroform, etc.
cards.quote: Benzoic acid, the simplest aromatic carboxylic acid is nearly insoluble in cold water. Carboxylic acids are also soluble in less polar organic solvents like benzene, ether, alcohol, chloroform, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do carboxylic acids differ from phenols in reacting with carbonates and hydrogencarbonates, and what is it used for?
cards.back: The carboxylic acids like alcohols evolve hydrogen with electropositive metals and form salts with alkalies similar to phenols. However, unlike phenols they react with weaker bases such as carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to evolve carbon dioxide. This reaction is used to detect the presence of carboxyl group in an organic compound.
cards.quote: The carboxylic acids like alcohols evolve hydrogen with electropositive metals and form salts with alkalies similar to phenols. However, unlike phenols they react with weaker bases such as carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to evolve carbon dioxide. This reaction is used to detect the presence of carboxyl group in an organic compound.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Carboxylic acids dissociate in water to give resonance stabilised carboxylate anions and ____.
cards.back: Carboxylic acids dissociate in water to give resonance stabilised carboxylate anions and hydronium ion.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids dissociate in water to give resonance stabilised carboxylate anions and hydronium ion.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In the dissociation of carboxylic acids, what are Keq and Ka?
cards.back: where Keq, is equilibrium constant and Ka is the acid dissociation constant.
cards.quote: where Keq, is equilibrium constant and Ka is the acid dissociation constant.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is the strength of an acid generally indicated?
cards.back: For convenience, the strength of an acid is generally indicated by its pKa value rather than its Ka value.
cards.quote: For convenience, the strength of an acid is generally indicated by its pKa value rather than its Ka value.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: pKa in terms of Ka.
cards.back: pKa = – log Ka
cards.quote: pKa = – log Ka

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the pKa values of hydrochloric acid, trifluoroacetic acid, benzoic acid and acetic acid?
cards.back: The pKa of hydrochloric acid is –7.0, where as pKa of trifluoroacetic acid (the strongest carboxylic acid), benzoic acid and acetic acid are 0.23, 4.19 and 4.76, respectively.
cards.quote: The pKa of hydrochloric acid is –7.0, where as pKa of trifluoroacetic acid (the strongest carboxylic acid), benzoic acid and acetic acid are 0.23, 4.19 and 4.76, respectively.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Smaller the pKa, the ____ the acid ( the better it is as a proton donor).
cards.back: Smaller the pKa, the stronger the acid ( the better it is as a proton donor).
cards.quote: Smaller the pKa, the stronger the acid ( the better it is as a proton donor).

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Classify acids as strong, moderately strong, weak and extremely weak by pKa value.
cards.back:
Strong acids have pKa values < 1
the acids with pKa values between 1 and 5 are considered to be moderately strong acids
weak acids have pKa values between 5 and 15
extremely weak acids have pKa values >15
cards.quote: Strong acids have pKa values < 1, the acids with pKa values between 1 and 5 are considered to be moderately strong acids, weak acids have pKa values between 5 and 15, and extremely weak acids have pKa values >15.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do carboxylic acids compare in strength with mineral acids, alcohols and phenols (pKa of ethanol and phenol)?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are weaker than mineral acids, but they are stronger acids than alcohols and many simple phenols (pKa is ~16 for ethanol and 10 for phenol).
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are weaker than mineral acids, but they are stronger acids than alcohols and many simple phenols (pKa is ~16 for ethanol and 10 for phenol).

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is a carboxylate ion more stable than a phenoxide ion (resonance structures)?
cards.back: The conjugate base of carboxylic acid, a carboxylate ion, is stabilised by two equivalent resonance structures in which the negative charge is at the more electronegative oxygen atom. The conjugate base of phenol, a phenoxide ion, has non-equivalent resonance structures in which the negative charge is at the less electronegative carbon atom.
cards.quote: The conjugate base of carboxylic acid, a carboxylate ion, is stabilised by two equivalent resonance structures in which the negative charge is at the more electronegative oxygen atom. The conjugate base of phenol, a phenoxide ion, has non-equivalent resonance structures in which the negative charge is at the less electronegative carbon atom.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is the negative charge delocalised in carboxylate ion compared with phenoxide ion?
cards.back: the negative charge is delocalised over two electronegative oxygen atoms in carboxylate ion whereas it is less effectively delocalised over one oxygen atom and less electronegative carbon atoms in phenoxide ion
cards.quote: the negative charge is delocalised over two electronegative oxygen atoms in carboxylate ion whereas it is less effectively delocalised over one oxygen atom and less electronegative carbon atoms in phenoxide ion

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why are carboxylic acids more acidic than phenols?
cards.back: Thus, the carboxylate ion is more stabilised than phenoxide ion, so carboxylic acids are more acidic than phenols.
cards.quote: Thus, the carboxylate ion is more stabilised than phenoxide ion, so carboxylic acids are more acidic than phenols.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do electron withdrawing groups affect the acidity of carboxylic acids?
cards.back: Electron withdrawing groups increase the acidity of carboxylic acids by stabilising the conjugate base through delocalisation of the negative charge by inductive and/or resonance effects.
cards.quote: Electron withdrawing groups increase the acidity of carboxylic acids by stabilising the conjugate base through delocalisation of the negative charge by inductive and/or resonance effects.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Electron withdrawing group (EWG) vs electron donating group (EDG): the effect on the carboxylate anion and acid strength.
cards.back: Electron withdrawing group (EWG) stabilises the carboxylate anion and strengthens the acid Electron donating group (EDG) destabilises the carboxylate anion and weakens the acid
cards.quote: Electron withdrawing group (EWG) stabilises the carboxylate anion and strengthens the acid Electron donating group (EDG) destabilises the carboxylate anion and weakens the acid

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Arrange in increasing order of effect on acidity: CF3, Br, Ph, NO2, Cl, I, CN, F.
cards.back: Ph < I < Br < Cl < F < CN < NO2 < CF3
cards.quote: Ph < I < Br < Cl < F < CN < NO2 < CF3

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Decreasing acidity (pKa based): NC-CH2COOH, CF3COOH, CHCl2COOH, NO2CH2COOH, CCl3COOH.
cards.back: CF3COOH > CCl3COOH > CHCl2COOH > NO2CH2COOH > NC-CH2COOH
cards.quote: CF3COOH > CCl3COOH > CHCl2COOH > NO2CH2COOH > NC-CH2COOH

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Decreasing acidity (pKa based): HCOOH, ClCH2COOH, FCH2COOH, ClCH2CH2COOH, BrCH2COOH.
cards.back: FCH2COOH > ClCH2COOH > BrCH2COOH > HCOOH > ClCH2CH2COOH
cards.quote: FCH2COOH > ClCH2COOH > BrCH2COOH > HCOOH > ClCH2CH2COOH

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Decreasing acidity (pKa based): CH3CH2COOH, CH3COOH, C6H5COOH, C6H5CH2COOH.
cards.back: C6H5COOH > C6H5CH2COOH > CH3COOH > CH3CH2COOH
cards.quote: C6H5COOH > C6H5CH2COOH > CH3COOH > CH3CH2COOH

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why does direct attachment of a phenyl or vinyl group to the carboxyl group increase acidity?
cards.back: This is because of greater electronegativity of sp2 hybridised carbon to which carboxyl carbon is attached.
cards.quote: This is because of greater electronegativity of sp2 hybridised carbon to which carboxyl carbon is attached.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do electron withdrawing and electron donating groups on the phenyl ring affect the acidity of aromatic carboxylic acids?
cards.back: The presence of electron withdrawing group on the phenyl of aromatic carboxylic acid increases their acidity while electron donating groups decrease their acidity.
cards.quote: The presence of electron withdrawing group on the phenyl of aromatic carboxylic acid increases their acidity while electron donating groups decrease their acidity.

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the pKa values of 4-methoxybenzoic acid and benzoic acid?
cards.back:
4-Methoxy benzoic acid (pKa = 4.46)
Benzoic acid (pKa = 4.19)
cards.quote: 4-Methoxy benzoic acid (pKa = 4.46) Benzoic acid (pKa = 4.19)

source.section: 8.9.1 Reactions Involving Cleavage of O–H Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is an anhydride formed from carboxylic acids?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids on heating with mineral acids such as H2SO4 or with P2O5 give corresponding anhydride.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids on heating with mineral acids such as H2SO4 or with P2O5 give corresponding anhydride.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Esterification: with which reagents and catalyst are carboxylic acids esterified?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are esterified with alcohols or phenols in the presence of a mineral acid such as concentrated H2SO4 or HCl gas as a catalyst.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are esterified with alcohols or phenols in the presence of a mineral acid such as concentrated H2SO4 or HCl gas as a catalyst.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The esterification of carboxylic acids with alcohols is a kind of ____.
cards.back: The esterification of carboxylic acids with alcohols is a kind of nucleophilic acyl substitution.
cards.quote: The esterification of carboxylic acids with alcohols is a kind of nucleophilic acyl substitution.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In the mechanism of esterification, what does protonation of the carbonyl oxygen achieve?
cards.back: Protonation of the carbonyl oxygen activates the carbonyl group towards nucleophilic addition of the alcohol.
cards.quote: Protonation of the carbonyl oxygen activates the carbonyl group towards nucleophilic addition of the alcohol.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which reagents replace the hydroxyl group of carboxylic acids by a chlorine atom?
cards.back: The hydroxyl group of carboxylic acids, behaves like that of alcohols and is easily replaced by chlorine atom on treating with PCl5, PCl3 or SOCl2.
cards.quote: The hydroxyl group of carboxylic acids, behaves like that of alcohols and is easily replaced by chlorine atom on treating with PCl5, PCl3 or SOCl2.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is thionyl chloride (SOCl2) preferred for converting carboxylic acids to acid chlorides?
cards.back: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) is preferred because the other two products are gaseous and escape the reaction mixture making the purification of the products easier.
cards.quote: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) is preferred because the other two products are gaseous and escape the reaction mixture making the purification of the products easier.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do carboxylic acids give with ammonia, and what on further heating?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids react with ammonia to give ammonium salt which on further heating at high temperature give amides.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids react with ammonia to give ammonium salt which on further heating at high temperature give amides.

source.section: 8.9.2 Reactions Involving Cleavage of C–OH Bond

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which reagents reduce carboxylic acids to primary alcohols?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by lithium aluminium hydride or better with diborane.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by lithium aluminium hydride or better with diborane.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which functional groups are not easily reduced by diborane?
cards.back: Diborane does not easily reduce functional groups such as ester, nitro, halo, etc.
cards.quote: Diborane does not easily reduce functional groups such as ester, nitro, halo, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Can sodium borohydride reduce the carboxyl group?
cards.back: Sodium borohydride does not reduce the carboxyl group.
cards.quote: Sodium borohydride does not reduce the carboxyl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Decarboxylation: how are hydrocarbons formed from sodium salts of carboxylic acids?
cards.back: Carboxylic acids lose carbon dioxide to form hydrocarbons when their sodium salts are heated with sodalime (NaOH and CaO in the ratio of 3 : 1). The reaction is known as decarboxylation.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids lose carbon dioxide to form hydrocarbons when their sodium salts are heated with sodalime (NaOH and CaO in the ratio of 3 : 1). The reaction is known as decarboxylation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction: electrolysis of alkali metal salts of carboxylic acids giving hydrocarbons with twice the carbon atoms.
cards.back: Alkali metal salts of carboxylic acids also undergo decarboxylation on electrolysis of their aqueous solutions and form hydrocarbons having twice the number of carbon atoms present in the alkyl group of the acid. The reaction is known as Kolbe electrolysis (Unit 9, Class XI).
cards.quote: Alkali metal salts of carboxylic acids also undergo decarboxylation on electrolysis of their aqueous solutions and form hydrocarbons having twice the number of carbon atoms present in the alkyl group of the acid. The reaction is known as Kolbe electrolysis (Unit 9, Class XI).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the reaction in which carboxylic acids with an α-hydrogen are halogenated at the α-position using Cl2 or Br2 and red phosphorus.
cards.back: Carboxylic acids having an α-hydrogen are halogenated at the α-position on treatment with chlorine or bromine in the presence of small amount of red phosphorus to give α-halocarboxylic acids. The reaction is known as Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.
cards.quote: Carboxylic acids having an α-hydrogen are halogenated at the α-position on treatment with chlorine or bromine in the presence of small amount of red phosphorus to give α-halocarboxylic acids. The reaction is known as Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

source.section: 8.9.4 Substitution Reactions in the Hydrocarbon Part

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do aromatic carboxylic acids undergo electrophilic substitution, and what is the role of the carboxyl group?
cards.back: Aromatic carboxylic acids undergo electrophilic substitution reactions in which the carboxyl group acts as a deactivating and meta-directing group.
cards.quote: Aromatic carboxylic acids undergo electrophilic substitution reactions in which the carboxyl group acts as a deactivating and meta-directing group.

source.section: 8.9.4 Substitution Reactions in the Hydrocarbon Part

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why do aromatic carboxylic acids not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction?
cards.back: They however, do not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (because the carboxyl group is deactivating and the catalyst aluminium chloride (Lewis acid) gets bonded to the carboxyl group).
cards.quote: They however, do not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (because the carboxyl group is deactivating and the catalyst aluminium chloride (Lewis acid) gets bonded to the carboxyl group).

source.section: 8.9.4 Substitution Reactions in the Hydrocarbon Part

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Methanoic acid is used in which industries?
cards.back: Methanoic acid is used in rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating industries.
cards.quote: Methanoic acid is used in rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating industries.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is ethanoic acid used as?
cards.back: Ethanoic acid is used as solvent and as vinegar in food industry.
cards.quote: Ethanoic acid is used as solvent and as vinegar in food industry.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Hexanedioic acid is used in the manufacture of ____.
cards.back: Hexanedioic acid is used in the manufacture of nylon-6, 6.
cards.quote: Hexanedioic acid is used in the manufacture of nylon-6, 6.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Esters of benzoic acid and sodium benzoate are used for what?
cards.back: Esters of benzoic acid are used in perfumery. Sodium benzoate is used as a food preservative.
cards.quote: Esters of benzoic acid are used in perfumery. Sodium benzoate is used as a food preservative.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Higher fatty acids are used for the manufacture of ____.
cards.back: Higher fatty acids are used for the manufacture of soaps and detergents.
cards.quote: Higher fatty acids are used for the manufacture of soaps and detergents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are amines?
cards.back: Amines can be considered as derivatives of ammonia, obtained by replacement of one, two or all the three hydrogen atoms by alkyl and/or aryl groups.
cards.quote: Amines can be considered as derivatives of ammonia, obtained by replacement of one, two or all the three hydrogen atoms by alkyl and/or aryl groups.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Quaternary ammonium salts are used as ____.
cards.back: Quaternary ammonium salts are used as surfactants.
cards.quote: Quaternary ammonium salts are used as surfactants.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Diazonium salts are ____ in the preparation of a variety of aromatic compounds including dyes.
cards.back: Diazonium salts are intermediates in the preparation of a variety of aromatic compounds including dyes.
cards.quote: Diazonium salts are intermediates in the preparation of a variety of aromatic compounds including dyes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Like ammonia, nitrogen atom of amines is ____ and carries an ____.
cards.back: Like ammonia, nitrogen atom of amines is trivalent and carries an unshared pair of electrons.
cards.quote: Like ammonia, nitrogen atom of amines is trivalent and carries an unshared pair of electrons.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Nitrogen orbitals in amines are therefore, ____ and the geometry of amines is ____.
cards.back: Nitrogen orbitals in amines are therefore, sp3 hybridised and the geometry of amines is pyramidal.
cards.quote: Nitrogen orbitals in amines are therefore, sp3 hybridised and the geometry of amines is pyramidal.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Types of amines on the basis of the number of hydrogen atoms of ammonia replaced
cards.back:
primary
secondary
tertiary
cards.quote: classify amines as primary, secondary and tertiary

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In common system, an aliphatic amine is named by prefixing alkyl group to amine, i.e., ____ as one word (e.g., methylamine).
cards.back: In common system, an aliphatic amine is named by prefixing alkyl group to amine, i.e., alkylamine as one word (e.g., methylamine).
cards.quote: In common system, an aliphatic amine is named by prefixing alkyl group to amine, i.e., alkylamine as one word (e.g., methylamine).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In IUPAC system, primary amines are named as ____. The name is derived by replacement of 'e' of alkane by the word amine.
cards.back: In IUPAC system, primary amines are named as alkanamines. The name is derived by replacement of 'e' of alkane by the word amine.
cards.quote: In IUPAC system, primary amines are named as alkanamines. The name is derived by replacement of 'e' of alkane by the word amine.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In secondary and tertiary amines, when two or more groups are the same, the prefix ____ is appended before the name of alkyl group.
cards.back: In secondary and tertiary amines, when two or more groups are the same, the prefix di or tri is appended before the name of alkyl group.
cards.quote: In secondary and tertiary amines, when two or more groups are the same, the prefix di or tri is appended before the name of alkyl group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC name of CH3NH2?
cards.back: methanamine
cards.quote: For example, CH3NH2 is named as methanamine.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: To name secondary and tertiary amines, we use ____ to designate substituent attached to a nitrogen atom.
cards.back: To name secondary and tertiary amines, we use locant N to designate substituent attached to a nitrogen atom.
cards.quote: To name secondary and tertiary amines, we use locant N to designate substituent attached to a nitrogen atom.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: IUPAC names of CH3NHCH2CH3 and (CH3CH2)3N?
cards.back:
N-methylethanamine
N, N-diethylethanamine
cards.quote: CH3NHCH2CH3 is named as N-methylethanamine and (CH3CH2)3N is named as N, N-diethylethanamine.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: C6H5NH2 is the simplest example of arylamine. In common system, it is known as ____. It is also an accepted IUPAC name.
cards.back: C6H5NH2 is the simplest example of arylamine. In common system, it is known as aniline. It is also an accepted IUPAC name.
cards.quote: C6H5NH2 is the simplest example of arylamine. In common system, it is known as aniline. It is also an accepted IUPAC name.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: While naming arylamines according to IUPAC system, suffix 'e' of ____ is replaced by 'amine'.
cards.back: While naming arylamines according to IUPAC system, suffix 'e' of arene is replaced by 'amine'.
cards.quote: While naming arylamines according to IUPAC system, suffix 'e' of arene is replaced by 'amine'.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Nitro compounds are reduced to amines by passing hydrogen gas in the presence of ____ and also by reduction with metals in acidic medium.
cards.back: Nitro compounds are reduced to amines by passing hydrogen gas in the presence of finely divided nickel, palladium or platinum and also by reduction with metals in acidic medium.
cards.quote: Nitro compounds are reduced to amines by passing hydrogen gas in the presence of finely divided nickel, palladium or platinum and also by reduction with metals in acidic medium.
blanks: finely divided nickel, palladium or platinum

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Reduction with ____ is preferred because FeCl2 formed gets hydrolysed to release hydrochloric acid during the reaction.
cards.back: Reduction with iron scrap and hydrochloric acid is preferred because FeCl2 formed gets hydrolysed to release hydrochloric acid during the reaction.
cards.quote: Reduction with iron scrap and hydrochloric acid is preferred because FeCl2 formed gets hydrolysed to release hydrochloric acid during the reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The free amine can be obtained from the ammonium salt by treatment with a ____:
cards.back: The free amine can be obtained from the ammonium salt by treatment with a strong base:
cards.quote: The free amine can be obtained from the ammonium salt by treatment with a strong base:

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Ammonolysis has the disadvantage of yielding a ____ of primary, secondary and tertiary amines and also a quaternary ammonium salt.
cards.back: Ammonolysis has the disadvantage of yielding a mixture of primary, secondary and tertiary amines and also a quaternary ammonium salt.
cards.quote: Ammonolysis has the disadvantage of yielding a mixture of primary, secondary and tertiary amines and also a quaternary ammonium salt.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The order of reactivity of halides with amines is ____.
cards.back: The order of reactivity of halides with amines is RI > RBr >RCl.
cards.quote: The order of reactivity of halides with amines is RI > RBr >RCl.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Nitriles on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4) or catalytic hydrogenation produce ____.
cards.back: Nitriles on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4) or catalytic hydrogenation produce primary amines.
cards.quote: Nitriles on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride (LiAlH4) or catalytic hydrogenation produce primary amines.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The amides on reduction with ____ yield amines.
cards.back: The amides on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride yield amines.
cards.quote: The amides on reduction with lithium aluminium hydride yield amines.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Gabriel synthesis is used for the preparation of ____.
cards.back: Gabriel synthesis is used for the preparation of primary amines.
cards.quote: Gabriel synthesis is used for the preparation of primary amines.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis of primary amines: steps in order
cards.back:
Phthalimide on treatment with ethanolic potassium hydroxide forms potassium salt of phthalimide
heating with alkyl halide
alkaline hydrolysis produces the corresponding primary amine
cards.quote: Phthalimide on treatment with ethanolic potassium hydroxide forms potassium salt of phthalimide which on heating with alkyl halide followed by alkaline hydrolysis produces the corresponding primary amine.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method because ____ do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.
cards.back: Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.
cards.quote: Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the anion formed by phthalimide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Hoffmann developed a method for preparation of primary amines by treating an amide with ____ in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide.
cards.back: Hoffmann developed a method for preparation of primary amines by treating an amide with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide.
cards.quote: Hoffmann developed a method for preparation of primary amines by treating an amide with bromine in an aqueous or ethanolic solution of sodium hydroxide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In this degradation reaction, migration of an alkyl or aryl group takes place from ____ of the amide to the nitrogen atom.
cards.back: In this degradation reaction, migration of an alkyl or aryl group takes place from carbonyl carbon of the amide to the nitrogen atom.
cards.quote: In this degradation reaction, migration of an alkyl or aryl group takes place from carbonyl carbon of the amide to the nitrogen atom.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The amine so formed contains ____ than that present in the amide.
cards.back: The amine so formed contains one carbon less than that present in the amide.
cards.quote: The amine so formed contains one carbon less than that present in the amide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The lower aliphatic amines are gases with ____.
cards.back: The lower aliphatic amines are gases with fishy odour.
cards.quote: The lower aliphatic amines are gases with fishy odour.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary amines with three or more carbon atoms are ____ and still higher ones are solid.
cards.back: Primary amines with three or more carbon atoms are liquid and still higher ones are solid.
cards.quote: Primary amines with three or more carbon atoms are liquid and still higher ones are solid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aniline and other arylamines are usually colourless but get coloured on storage due to ____.
cards.back: Aniline and other arylamines are usually colourless but get coloured on storage due to atmospheric oxidation.
cards.quote: Aniline and other arylamines are usually colourless but get coloured on storage due to atmospheric oxidation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water because they can form ____ with water molecules.
cards.back: Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water because they can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.
cards.quote: Lower aliphatic amines are soluble in water because they can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Higher amines are essentially ____ in water.
cards.back: Higher amines are essentially insoluble in water.
cards.quote: Higher amines are essentially insoluble in water.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: You may remember that ____ are more polar than amines and form stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonds than amines.
cards.back: You may remember that alcohols are more polar than amines and form stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonds than amines.
cards.quote: You may remember that alcohols are more polar than amines and form stronger intermolecular hydrogen bonds than amines.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary and secondary amines are engaged in ____ due to hydrogen bonding between nitrogen of one and hydrogen of another molecule.
cards.back: Primary and secondary amines are engaged in intermolecular association due to hydrogen bonding between nitrogen of one and hydrogen of another molecule.
cards.quote: Primary and secondary amines are engaged in intermolecular association due to hydrogen bonding between nitrogen of one and hydrogen of another molecule.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Tertiary amines do not have intermolecular association due to the ____ available for hydrogen bond formation.
cards.back: Tertiary amines do not have intermolecular association due to the absence of hydrogen atom available for hydrogen bond formation.
cards.quote: Tertiary amines do not have intermolecular association due to the absence of hydrogen atom available for hydrogen bond formation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amines, being basic in nature, react with acids to form ____.
cards.back: Amines, being basic in nature, react with acids to form salts.
cards.quote: Amines, being basic in nature, react with acids to form salts.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amine salts on treatment with a base like NaOH, ____.
cards.back: Amine salts on treatment with a base like NaOH, regenerate the parent amine.
cards.quote: Amine salts on treatment with a base like NaOH, regenerate the parent amine.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amine salts are soluble in water but ____ like ether.
cards.back: Amine salts are soluble in water but insoluble in organic solvents like ether.
cards.quote: Amine salts are soluble in water but insoluble in organic solvents like ether.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amines have an unshared pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as ____.
cards.back: Amines have an unshared pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as Lewis base.
cards.quote: Amines have an unshared pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as Lewis base.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Larger the value of Kb or ____, stronger is the base.
cards.back: Larger the value of Kb or smaller the value of pKb, stronger is the base.
cards.quote: Larger the value of Kb or smaller the value of pKb, stronger is the base.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: pKb value of ammonia is ____.
cards.back: pKb value of ammonia is 4.75.
cards.quote: pKb value of ammonia is 4.75.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia due to ____ of alkyl groups leading to high electron density on the nitrogen atom.
cards.back: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia due to +I effect of alkyl groups leading to high electron density on the nitrogen atom.
cards.quote: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia due to +I effect of alkyl groups leading to high electron density on the nitrogen atom.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The order of basicity of amines in the gaseous phase follows the expected order: ____.
cards.back: The order of basicity of amines in the gaseous phase follows the expected order: tertiary amine > secondary amine > primary amine > NH3.
cards.quote: The order of basicity of amines in the gaseous phase follows the expected order: tertiary amine > secondary amine > primary amine > NH3.
blanks: tertiary amine > secondary amine > primary amine > NH3

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The greater the size of the ion, ____ and the less stabilised is the ion.
cards.back: The greater the size of the ion, lesser will be the solvation and the less stabilised is the ion.
cards.quote: The greater the size of the ion, lesser will be the solvation and the less stabilised is the ion.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Basic strength order of ethyl substituted amines and NH3 in aqueous solution?
cards.back: (C2H5)2NH > (C2H5)3N > C2H5NH2 > NH3
cards.quote: (C2H5)2NH > (C2H5)3N > C2H5NH2 > NH3

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Basic strength order of methyl substituted amines and NH3 in aqueous solution?
cards.back: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N > NH3
cards.quote: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N > NH3

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: If you write different resonating structures of aniline, you will find that aniline is a resonance hybrid of the following ____ structures.
cards.back: If you write different resonating structures of aniline, you will find that aniline is a resonance hybrid of the following five structures.
cards.quote: If you write different resonating structures of aniline, you will find that aniline is a resonance hybrid of the following five structures.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively ____ their basic character.
cards.back: In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character.
cards.quote: In aromatic amines, electron releasing and withdrawing groups, respectively increase and decrease their basic character.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Decreasing basic strength: C6H5NH2, C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, NH3?
cards.back: (C2H5)2NH > C2H5NH2 > NH3 > C6H5NH2
cards.quote: (C2H5)2NH > C2H5NH2 > NH3 > C6H5NH2

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is acylation of amines?
cards.back: Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. This reaction is known as acylation.
cards.quote: Aliphatic and aromatic primary and secondary amines react with acid chlorides, anhydrides and esters by nucleophilic substitution reaction. This reaction is known as acylation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The products obtained by acylation reaction are known as ____.
cards.back: The products obtained by acylation reaction are known as amides.
cards.quote: The products obtained by acylation reaction are known as amides.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amines also react with benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl). This reaction is known as ____.
cards.back: Amines also react with benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl). This reaction is known as benzoylation.
cards.quote: Amines also react with benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl). This reaction is known as benzoylation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with ____ form isocyanides or carbylamines which are foul smelling substances.
cards.back: Aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide form isocyanides or carbylamines which are foul smelling substances.
cards.quote: Aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide form isocyanides or carbylamines which are foul smelling substances.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Three classes of amines react differently with nitrous acid which is prepared in situ from a ____.
cards.back: Three classes of amines react differently with nitrous acid which is prepared in situ from a mineral acid and sodium nitrite.
cards.quote: Three classes of amines react differently with nitrous acid which is prepared in situ from a mineral acid and sodium nitrite.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to form aliphatic diazonium salts which being unstable, liberate ____ quantitatively and alcohols.
cards.back: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to form aliphatic diazonium salts which being unstable, liberate nitrogen gas quantitatively and alcohols.
cards.quote: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to form aliphatic diazonium salts which being unstable, liberate nitrogen gas quantitatively and alcohols.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Quantitative evolution of nitrogen is used in ____.
cards.back: Quantitative evolution of nitrogen is used in estimation of amino acids and proteins.
cards.quote: Quantitative evolution of nitrogen is used in estimation of amino acids and proteins.
blanks: estimation of amino acids and proteins

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aromatic amines react with nitrous acid at low temperatures (____) to form diazonium salts
cards.back: Aromatic amines react with nitrous acid at low temperatures (273-278 K) to form diazonium salts
cards.quote: Aromatic amines react with nitrous acid at low temperatures (273-278 K) to form diazonium salts

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl), which is also known as ____, reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulphonamides.
cards.back: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl), which is also known as Hinsberg's reagent, reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulphonamides.
cards.quote: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl), which is also known as Hinsberg's reagent, reacts with primary and secondary amines to form sulphonamides.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Since N, N-diethylbenzene sulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence ____.
cards.back: Since N, N-diethylbenzene sulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence insoluble in alkali.
cards.quote: Since N, N-diethylbenzene sulphonamide does not contain any hydrogen atom attached to nitrogen atom, it is not acidic and hence insoluble in alkali.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: ____ do not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
cards.back: Tertiary amines do not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride.
cards.quote: Tertiary amines do not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Directing and activating effect of the -NH2 group in aniline?
cards.back: ortho and para directing and a powerful activating group
cards.quote: ortho and para directing and a powerful activating group

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of ____.
cards.back: Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
cards.quote: Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their ____.
cards.back: The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their very high reactivity.
cards.quote: The main problem encountered during electrophilic substitution reactions of aromatic amines is that of their very high reactivity.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Controlling the activating effect of the amino group in aniline: steps in order
cards.back:
acetylation with acetic anhydride
carrying out the desired substitution
hydrolysis of the substituted amide to the substituted amine
cards.quote: acetylation with acetic anhydride, then carrying out the desired substitution followed by hydrolysis of the substituted amide to the substituted amine

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Direct nitration of aniline yields ____ in addition to the nitro derivatives.
cards.back: Direct nitration of aniline yields tarry oxidation products in addition to the nitro derivatives.
cards.quote: Direct nitration of aniline yields tarry oxidation products in addition to the nitro derivatives.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: That is why besides the ortho and para derivatives, significant amount of ____ is also formed.
cards.back: That is why besides the ortho and para derivatives, significant amount of meta derivative is also formed.
cards.quote: That is why besides the ortho and para derivatives, significant amount of meta derivative is also formed.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acetylation) due to ____, the Lewis acid, which is used as a catalyst.
cards.back: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acetylation) due to salt formation with aluminium chloride, the Lewis acid, which is used as a catalyst.
cards.quote: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction (alkylation and acetylation) due to salt formation with aluminium chloride, the Lewis acid, which is used as a catalyst.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires positive charge and hence acts as a ____ for further reaction.
cards.back: Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires positive charge and hence acts as a strong deactivating group for further reaction.
cards.quote: Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires positive charge and hence acts as a strong deactivating group for further reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary aliphatic amines form ____ alkyldiazonium salts
cards.back: Primary aliphatic amines form highly unstable alkyldiazonium salts
cards.quote: Primary aliphatic amines form highly unstable alkyldiazonium salts

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Primary aromatic amines form ____ which are stable for a short time in solution at low temperatures (273-278 K).
cards.back: Primary aromatic amines form arenediazonium salts which are stable for a short time in solution at low temperatures (273-278 K).
cards.quote: Primary aromatic amines form arenediazonium salts which are stable for a short time in solution at low temperatures (273-278 K).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The stability of arenediazonium ion is explained on the basis of ____.
cards.back: The stability of arenediazonium ion is explained on the basis of resonance.
cards.quote: The stability of arenediazonium ion is explained on the basis of resonance.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at ____.
cards.back: Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278K.
cards.quote: Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278K.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Nitrous acid is produced in the reaction mixture by the reaction of ____.
cards.back: Nitrous acid is produced in the reaction mixture by the reaction of sodium nitrite with hydrochloric acid.
cards.quote: Nitrous acid is produced in the reaction mixture by the reaction of sodium nitrite with hydrochloric acid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define diazotisation.
cards.back: The conversion of primary aromatic amines into diazonium salts is known as diazotisation.
cards.quote: The conversion of primary aromatic amines into diazonium salts is known as diazotisation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Due to its instability, the diazonium salt is not generally stored and is ____ after its preparation.
cards.back: Due to its instability, the diazonium salt is not generally stored and is used immediately after its preparation.
cards.quote: Due to its instability, the diazonium salt is not generally stored and is used immediately after its preparation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Benzenediazonium chloride is a ____.
cards.back: Benzenediazonium chloride is a colourless crystalline solid.
cards.quote: Benzenediazonium chloride is a colourless crystalline solid.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is ____ and stable at room temperature.
cards.back: Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is water insoluble and stable at room temperature.
cards.quote: Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is water insoluble and stable at room temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Two categories of reactions of diazonium salts
cards.back:
reactions involving displacement of nitrogen
reactions involving retention of diazo group
cards.quote: The reactions of diazonium salts can be broadly divided into two categories, namely (A) reactions involving displacement of nitrogen and (B) reactions involving retention of diazo group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name of the reaction in which Cl-, Br- and CN- replace the diazonium group in the presence of Cu(I) ion?
cards.back: Sandmeyer reaction
cards.quote: in the presence of Cu(I) ion. This reaction is called Sandmeyer reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Reaction: chlorine or bromine introduced by diazonium salt with halogen acid and copper powder?
cards.back: Gatterman reaction
cards.quote: treating the diazonium salt solution with corresponding halogen acid in the presence of copper powder. This is referred as Gatterman reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The yield in ____ reaction is found to be better than Gattermann reaction.
cards.back: The yield in Sandmeyer reaction is found to be better than Gattermann reaction.
cards.quote: The yield in Sandmeyer reaction is found to be better than Gattermann reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Iodine is not easily introduced into the benzene ring directly, but, when the diazonium salt solution is treated with ____, iodobenzene is formed.
cards.back: Iodine is not easily introduced into the benzene ring directly, but, when the diazonium salt solution is treated with potassium iodide, iodobenzene is formed.
cards.quote: Iodine is not easily introduced into the benzene ring directly, but, when the diazonium salt solution is treated with potassium iodide, iodobenzene is formed.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When arenediazonium chloride is treated with ____, arene diazonium fluoroborate is precipitated which on heating decomposes to yield aryl fluoride.
cards.back: When arenediazonium chloride is treated with fluoroboric acid, arene diazonium fluoroborate is precipitated which on heating decomposes to yield aryl fluoride.
cards.quote: When arenediazonium chloride is treated with fluoroboric acid, arene diazonium fluoroborate is precipitated which on heating decomposes to yield aryl fluoride.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Certain mild reducing agents like ____ reduce diazonium salts to arenes and themselves get oxidised to phosphorous acid and ethanal, respectively.
cards.back: Certain mild reducing agents like hypophosphorous acid (phosphinic acid) or ethanol reduce diazonium salts to arenes and themselves get oxidised to phosphorous acid and ethanal, respectively.
cards.quote: Certain mild reducing agents like hypophosphorous acid (phosphinic acid) or ethanol reduce diazonium salts to arenes and themselves get oxidised to phosphorous acid and ethanal, respectively.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: If the temperature of the diazonium salt solution is allowed to rise upto ____, the salt gets hydrolysed to phenol.
cards.back: If the temperature of the diazonium salt solution is allowed to rise upto 283 K, the salt gets hydrolysed to phenol.
cards.quote: If the temperature of the diazonium salt solution is allowed to rise upto 283 K, the salt gets hydrolysed to phenol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is diazonium fluoroborate heated with, in presence of copper, to replace the diazonium group by -NO2?
cards.back: aqueous sodium nitrite solution
cards.quote: When diazonium fluoroborate is heated with aqueous sodium nitrite solution in the presence of copper

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a coupling reaction of a diazonium salt?
cards.back: Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol in which the phenol molecule at its para position is coupled with the diazonium salt to form p-hydroxyazobenzene. This type of reaction is known as coupling reaction.
cards.quote: Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol in which the phenol molecule at its para position is coupled with the diazonium salt to form p-hydroxyazobenzene. This type of reaction is known as coupling reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Similarly the reaction of diazonium salt with aniline yields ____.
cards.back: Similarly the reaction of diazonium salt with aniline yields p-aminoazobenzene.
cards.quote: Similarly the reaction of diazonium salt with aniline yields p-aminoazobenzene.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Coupling reaction of aryldiazonium salts with phenols or arylamines give rise to the formation of ____.
cards.back: Coupling reaction of aryldiazonium salts with phenols or arylamines give rise to the formation of azo dyes.
cards.quote: Coupling reaction of aryldiazonium salts with phenols or arylamines give rise to the formation of azo dyes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The cyano group cannot be introduced by nucleophilic substitution of chlorine in chlorobenzene but cyanobenzene can be easily obtained from ____.
cards.back: The cyano group cannot be introduced by nucleophilic substitution of chlorine in chlorobenzene but cyanobenzene can be easily obtained from diazonium salt.
cards.quote: The cyano group cannot be introduced by nucleophilic substitution of chlorine in chlorobenzene but cyanobenzene can be easily obtained from diazonium salt.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Tertiary amines like trimethylamine are used as ____.
cards.back: Tertiary amines like trimethylamine are used as insect attractants.
cards.quote: Tertiary amines like trimethylamine are used as insect attractants.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Reactivity of aromatic amines can be controlled by ____ process, i.e., by treating with acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride.
cards.back: Reactivity of aromatic amines can be controlled by acylation process, i.e., by treating with acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride.
cards.quote: Reactivity of aromatic amines can be controlled by acylation process, i.e., by treating with acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Alkyl amines are found to be ____ bases than ammonia.
cards.back: Alkyl amines are found to be stronger bases than ammonia.
cards.quote: Alkyl amines are found to be stronger bases than ammonia.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How are carbohydrates defined chemically?
cards.back: Chemically, the carbohydrates may be defined as optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or the compounds which produce such units on hydrolysis.
cards.quote: Chemically, the carbohydrates may be defined as optically active polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones or the compounds which produce such units on hydrolysis.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: General formula of most carbohydrates
cards.back: Cx(H2O)y
cards.quote: Most of them have a general formula, Cx(H2O)y, and were considered as hydrates of carbon from where the name carbohydrate was derived.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Acetic acid (CH3COOH) fits the formula Cx(H2O)y. Is it a carbohydrate?
cards.back: For example acetic acid (CH3COOH) fits into this general formula, C2(H2O)2 but is not a carbohydrate.
cards.quote: For example acetic acid (CH3COOH) fits into this general formula, C2(H2O)2 but is not a carbohydrate.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Some of the carbohydrates, which are sweet in taste, are also called ____.
cards.back: Some of the carbohydrates, which are sweet in taste, are also called sugars.
cards.quote: Some of the carbohydrates, which are sweet in taste, are also called sugars.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The most common sugar, used in our homes is named as ____
cards.back: The most common sugar, used in our homes is named as sucrose
cards.quote: The most common sugar, used in our homes is named as sucrose

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Carbohydrates are classified on the basis of their behaviour on ____.
cards.back: Carbohydrates are classified on the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis.
cards.quote: Carbohydrates are classified on the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a monosaccharide?
cards.back: A carbohydrate that cannot be hydrolysed further to give simpler unit of polyhydroxy aldehyde or ketone is called a monosaccharide.
cards.quote: A carbohydrate that cannot be hydrolysed further to give simpler unit of polyhydroxy aldehyde or ketone is called a monosaccharide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name three common examples of monosaccharides.
cards.back:
glucose
fructose
ribose
cards.quote: Some common examples are glucose, fructose, ribose, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are oligosaccharides?
cards.back: Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units, on hydrolysis, are called oligosaccharides.
cards.quote: Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units, on hydrolysis, are called oligosaccharides.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do sucrose and maltose give on hydrolysis?
cards.back: For example, one molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives one molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose whereas maltose gives two molecules of only glucose.
cards.quote: For example, one molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives one molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose whereas maltose gives two molecules of only glucose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are polysaccharides?
cards.back: Carbohydrates which yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called polysaccharides.
cards.quote: Carbohydrates which yield a large number of monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called polysaccharides.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name common examples of polysaccharides.
cards.back:
starch
cellulose
glycogen
gums
cards.quote: Some common examples are starch, cellulose, glycogen, gums, etc.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Polysaccharides are not sweet in taste, hence they are also called ____.
cards.back: Polysaccharides are not sweet in taste, hence they are also called non-sugars.
cards.quote: Polysaccharides are not sweet in taste, hence they are also called non-sugars.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are reducing sugars?
cards.back: All those carbohydrates which reduce Fehling’s solution and Tollens’ reagent are referred to as reducing sugars.
cards.quote: All those carbohydrates which reduce Fehling’s solution and Tollens’ reagent are referred to as reducing sugars.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: All monosaccharides whether aldose or ketose are ____ sugars.
cards.back: All monosaccharides whether aldose or ketose are reducing sugars.
cards.quote: All monosaccharides whether aldose or ketose are reducing sugars.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are an aldose and a ketose?
cards.back: If a monosaccharide contains an aldehyde group, it is known as an aldose and if it contains a keto group, it is known as a ketose.
cards.quote: If a monosaccharide contains an aldehyde group, it is known as an aldose and if it contains a keto group, it is known as a ketose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: General terms for monosaccharides with 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 carbon atoms
cards.back:
Triose
Tetrose
Pentose
Hexose
Heptose
cards.quote: 3 Triose Aldotriose Ketotriose 4 Tetrose Aldotetrose Ketotetrose 5 Pentose Aldopentose Ketopentose 6 Hexose Aldohexose Ketohexose 7 Heptose Aldoheptose Ketoheptose

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are obtained when sucrose is boiled with dilute HCl or H2SO4 in alcoholic solution?
cards.back: If sucrose is boiled with dilute HCl or H2SO4 in alcoholic solution, glucose and fructose are obtained in equal amounts.
cards.quote: If sucrose is boiled with dilute HCl or H2SO4 in alcoholic solution, glucose and fructose are obtained in equal amounts.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is glucose obtained commercially?
cards.back: Commercially glucose is obtained by hydrolysis of starch by boiling it with dilute H2SO4 at 393 K under pressure.
cards.quote: Commercially glucose is obtained by hydrolysis of starch by boiling it with dilute H2SO4 at 393 K under pressure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Glucose is an aldohexose and is also known as ____.
cards.back: Glucose is an aldohexose and is also known as dextrose.
cards.quote: Glucose is an aldohexose and is also known as dextrose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Glucose is the monomer of which larger carbohydrates?
cards.back: starch, cellulose
cards.quote: It is the monomer of many of the larger carbohydrates, namely starch, cellulose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Molecular formula of glucose
cards.back: C6H12O6
cards.quote: Its molecular formula was found to be C6H12O6.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does glucose form on prolonged heating with HI, and what does this suggest?
cards.back: On prolonged heating with HI, it forms n-hexane, suggesting that all the six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.
cards.quote: On prolonged heating with HI, it forms n-hexane, suggesting that all the six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do the reactions of glucose with hydroxylamine and hydrogen cyanide confirm?
cards.back: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime and adds a molecule of hydrogen cyanide to give cyanohydrin. These reactions confirm the presence of a carbonyl group (>C = O) in glucose.
cards.quote: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime and adds a molecule of hydrogen cyanide to give cyanohydrin. These reactions confirm the presence of a carbonyl group (>C = O) in glucose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Glucose is oxidised by bromine water to gluconic acid. What does this indicate?
cards.back: Glucose gets oxidised to six carbon carboxylic acid (gluconic acid) on reaction with a mild oxidising agent like bromine water. This indicates that the carbonyl group is present as an aldehydic group.
cards.quote: Glucose gets oxidised to six carbon carboxylic acid (gluconic acid) on reaction with a mild oxidising agent like bromine water. This indicates that the carbonyl group is present as an aldehydic group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride confirm?
cards.back: Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate which confirms the presence of five –OH groups.
cards.quote: Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate which confirms the presence of five –OH groups.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Glucose on oxidation with nitric acid yields saccharic acid. What does this indicate?
cards.back: On oxidation with nitric acid, glucose as well as gluconic acid both yield a dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid. This indicates the presence of a primary alcoholic (–OH) group in glucose.
cards.quote: On oxidation with nitric acid, glucose as well as gluconic acid both yield a dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid. This indicates the presence of a primary alcoholic (–OH) group in glucose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do ‘D’ and ‘(+)’ represent in the name D(+)-glucose?
cards.back: Glucose is correctly named as D(+)-glucose. ‘D’ before the name of glucose represents the configuration whereas ‘(+)’ represents dextrorotatory nature of the molecule.
cards.quote: Glucose is correctly named as D(+)-glucose. ‘D’ before the name of glucose represents the configuration whereas ‘(+)’ represents dextrorotatory nature of the molecule.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: ‘D’ and ‘L’ have no relation with the ____ of the compound.
cards.back: ‘D’ and ‘L’ have no relation with the optical activity of the compound.
cards.quote: ‘D’ and ‘L’ have no relation with the optical activity of the compound.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do the letters ‘D’ or ‘L’ before the name of a compound indicate?
cards.back: The letters ‘D’ or ‘L’ before the name of any compound indicate the relative configuration of a particular stereoisomer of a compound with respect to configuration of some other compound, configuration of which is known.
cards.quote: The letters ‘D’ or ‘L’ before the name of any compound indicate the relative configuration of a particular stereoisomer of a compound with respect to configuration of some other compound, configuration of which is known.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In carbohydrates, the D and L notation refers to the relation with an isomer of which compound?
cards.back: glyceraldehyde
cards.quote: In the case of carbohydrates, this refers to their relation with a particular isomer of glyceraldehyde.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which configuration does the (+) isomer of glyceraldehyde have?
cards.back: (+) Isomer of glyceraldehyde has ‘D’ configuration.
cards.quote: (+) Isomer of glyceraldehyde has ‘D’ configuration.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which compounds are said to have D-configuration and which L-configuration?
cards.back: All those compounds which can be chemically correlated to D (+) isomer of glyceraldehyde are said to have D-configuration whereas those which can be correlated to ‘L’ (–) isomer of glyceraldehyde are said to have L-configuration.
cards.quote: All those compounds which can be chemically correlated to D (+) isomer of glyceraldehyde are said to have D-configuration whereas those which can be correlated to ‘L’ (–) isomer of glyceraldehyde are said to have L-configuration.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In the L (–) isomer of glyceraldehyde, on which side is the –OH group?
cards.back: In L (–) isomer –OH group is on left hand side as you can see in the structure.
cards.quote: In L (–) isomer –OH group is on left hand side as you can see in the structure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: For assigning the configuration of monosaccharides, it is the ____ (as shown below) which is compared.
cards.back: For assigning the configuration of monosaccharides, it is the lowest asymmetric carbon atom (as shown below) which is compared.
cards.quote: For assigning the configuration of monosaccharides, it is the lowest asymmetric carbon atom (as shown below) which is compared.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is (+) glucose assigned D-configuration?
cards.back: As in (+) glucose, —OH on the lowest asymmetric carbon is on the right side which is comparable to (+) glyceraldehyde, so (+) glucose is assigned D-configuration.
cards.quote: As in (+) glucose, —OH on the lowest asymmetric carbon is on the right side which is comparable to (+) glyceraldehyde, so (+) glucose is assigned D-configuration.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Despite having an aldehyde group, which test and which addition product does glucose not give?
cards.back: Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give Schiff’s test and it does not form the hydrogensulphite addition product with NaHSO3.
cards.quote: Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give Schiff’s test and it does not form the hydrogensulphite addition product with NaHSO3.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does the non-reaction of glucose pentaacetate with hydroxylamine indicate?
cards.back: The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine indicating the absence of free —CHO group.
cards.quote: The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine indicating the absence of free —CHO group.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What was proposed to explain the properties of glucose that the open chain structure could not?
cards.back: It was proposed that one of the —OH groups may add to the —CHO group and form a cyclic hemiacetal structure.
cards.quote: It was proposed that one of the —OH groups may add to the —CHO group and form a cyclic hemiacetal structure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which –OH group of glucose takes part in forming its six-membered ring?
cards.back: It was found that glucose forms a six-membered ring in which —OH at C-5 is involved in ring formation.
cards.quote: It was found that glucose forms a six-membered ring in which —OH at C-5 is involved in ring formation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: With what do the two cyclic forms of glucose exist in equilibrium?
cards.back: open chain structure
cards.quote: These two cyclic forms exist in equilibrium with open chain structure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How do the two cyclic forms of glucose differ, and what is C1 called?
cards.back: The two cyclic hemiacetal forms of glucose differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C1, called anomeric carbon (the aldehyde carbon before cyclisation).
cards.quote: The two cyclic hemiacetal forms of glucose differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C1, called anomeric carbon (the aldehyde carbon before cyclisation).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The six membered cyclic structure of glucose is called ____ structure
cards.back: The six membered cyclic structure of glucose is called pyranose structure
cards.quote: The six membered cyclic structure of glucose is called pyranose structure

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How is fructose obtained?
cards.back: It is obtained along with glucose by the hydrolysis of disaccharide, sucrose.
cards.quote: It is obtained along with glucose by the hydrolysis of disaccharide, sucrose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Where is the ketonic functional group in fructose (molecular formula C6H12O6)?
cards.back: Fructose also has the molecular formula C6H12O6 and on the basis of its reactions it was found to contain a ketonic functional group at carbon number 2 and six carbons in straight chain as in the case of glucose.
cards.quote: Fructose also has the molecular formula C6H12O6 and on the basis of its reactions it was found to contain a ketonic functional group at carbon number 2 and six carbons in straight chain as in the case of glucose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: To which series does fructose belong, and how is it appropriately written?
cards.back: It belongs to D-series and is a laevorotatory compound. It is appropriately written as D-(–)-fructose.
cards.quote: It belongs to D-series and is a laevorotatory compound. It is appropriately written as D-(–)-fructose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The ring, thus formed is a five membered ring and is named as ____ with analogy to the compound furan.
cards.back: The ring, thus formed is a five membered ring and is named as furanose with analogy to the compound furan.
cards.quote: The ring, thus formed is a five membered ring and is named as furanose with analogy to the compound furan.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a glycosidic linkage?
cards.back: The two monosaccharides are joined together by an oxide linkage formed by the loss of a water molecule. Such a linkage between two monosaccharide units through oxygen atom is called glycosidic linkage.
cards.quote: The two monosaccharides are joined together by an oxide linkage formed by the loss of a water molecule. Such a linkage between two monosaccharide units through oxygen atom is called glycosidic linkage.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do disaccharides yield on hydrolysis with dilute acids or enzymes?
cards.back: disaccharides on hydrolysis with dilute acids or enzymes yield two molecules of either the same or different monosaccharides.
cards.quote: disaccharides on hydrolysis with dilute acids or enzymes yield two molecules of either the same or different monosaccharides.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When is a disaccharide a non-reducing sugar? Give an example.
cards.back: In disaccharides, if the reducing groups of monosaccharides i.e., aldehydic or ketonic groups are bonded, these are non-reducing sugars, e.g., sucrose.
cards.quote: In disaccharides, if the reducing groups of monosaccharides i.e., aldehydic or ketonic groups are bonded, these are non-reducing sugars, e.g., sucrose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which disaccharides, with free aldehydic or ketonic groups, are reducing sugars?
cards.back: On the other hand, sugars in which these functional groups are free, are called reducing sugars, for example, maltose and lactose.
cards.quote: On the other hand, sugars in which these functional groups are free, are called reducing sugars, for example, maltose and lactose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does sucrose give on hydrolysis?
cards.back: One of the common disaccharides is sucrose which on hydrolysis gives equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-) fructose.
cards.quote: One of the common disaccharides is sucrose which on hydrolysis gives equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-) fructose.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is the mixture from hydrolysis of dextrorotatory sucrose laevorotatory?
cards.back: Since the laevorotation of fructose (–92.4°) is more than dextrorotation of glucose (+ 52.5°), the mixture is laevorotatory.
cards.quote: Since the laevorotation of fructose (–92.4°) is more than dextrorotation of glucose (+ 52.5°), the mixture is laevorotatory.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Hydrolysis of sucrose brings about a change in the sign of rotation, from dextro (+) to laevo (–) and the product is named as ____.
cards.back: hydrolysis of sucrose brings about a change in the sign of rotation, from dextro (+) to laevo (–) and the product is named as invert sugar.
cards.quote: hydrolysis of sucrose brings about a change in the sign of rotation, from dextro (+) to laevo (–) and the product is named as invert sugar.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is maltose a reducing sugar?
cards.back: The free aldehyde group can be produced at C1 of second glucose in solution and it shows reducing properties so it is a reducing sugar.
cards.quote: The free aldehyde group can be produced at C1 of second glucose in solution and it shows reducing properties so it is a reducing sugar.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which disaccharide is more commonly known as milk sugar?
cards.back: Lactose: It is more commonly known as milk sugar since this disaccharide is found in milk.
cards.quote: Lactose: It is more commonly known as milk sugar since this disaccharide is found in milk.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In lactose, between which carbons is the linkage, and is it a reducing sugar?
cards.back: The linkage is between C1 of galactose and C4 of glucose. Free aldehyde group may be produced at C-1 of glucose unit, hence it is also a reducing sugar.
cards.quote: The linkage is between C1 of galactose and C4 of glucose. Free aldehyde group may be produced at C-1 of glucose unit, hence it is also a reducing sugar.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Polysaccharides contain a large number of monosaccharide units joined together by ____.
cards.back: Polysaccharides contain a large number of monosaccharide units joined together by glycosidic linkages.
cards.quote: Polysaccharides contain a large number of monosaccharide units joined together by glycosidic linkages.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What do polysaccharides mainly act as?
cards.back: food storage or structural materials
cards.quote: They mainly act as the food storage or structural materials.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is starch?
cards.back: Starch is the main storage polysaccharide of plants.
cards.quote: Starch is the main storage polysaccharide of plants.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Where is a high content of starch found?
cards.back: High content of starch is found in cereals, roots, tubers and some vegetables.
cards.quote: High content of starch is found in cereals, roots, tubers and some vegetables.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Starch consists of which two components?
cards.back:
Amylose
Amylopectin
cards.quote: consists of two components— Amylose and Amylopectin.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amylose: solubility in water and share of starch
cards.back: Amylose is water soluble component which constitutes about 15-20% of starch.
cards.quote: Amylose is water soluble component which constitutes about 15-20% of starch.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Amylopectin: solubility in water and share of starch
cards.back: Amylopectin is insoluble in water and constitutes about 80-85% of starch.
cards.quote: Amylopectin is insoluble in water and constitutes about 80-85% of starch.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Where does cellulose occur, and how abundant is it?
