cards.quote: A substitution reaction takes place and halogen atom, called leaving group departs as halide ion.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 6.4: class of main product from R-X with, in order, NaOH (KOH), H2O, NaOR', NaI, NH3, R'NH2, R'R''NH.
cards.back:
Alcohol
Alcohol
Ether
Alkyl iodide
Primary amine
Sec. amine
Tert. amine
cards.quote: Alcohol Alcohol Ether Alkyl iodide Primary amine Sec. amine Tert. amine

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 6.4: class of main product from R-X with, in order, KCN, AgCN, KNO2, AgNO2, R'COOAg, LiAlH4, R''M+.
cards.back:
Nitrile (cyanide)
Isonitrile
Alkyl nitrite
Nitroalkane
Ester
Hydrocarbon
Alkane
cards.quote: Nitrile (cyanide) Isonitrile Alkyl nitrite Nitroalkane Ester Hydrocarbon Alkane

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define ambident nucleophiles.
cards.back: Groups like cyanides and nitrites possess two nucleophilic centres and are called ambident nucleophiles.
cards.quote: Groups like cyanides and nitrites possess two nucleophilic centres and are called ambident nucleophiles.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form ____ as main product while AgCN forms ____ as the chief product.
cards.back: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as main product while AgCN forms isocyanides as the chief product.
cards.quote: Haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as main product while AgCN forms isocyanides as the chief product.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why does cyanide ion attack mainly through carbon, not nitrogen, in KCN?
cards.back: the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C-C bond is more stable than C-N bond.
cards.quote: Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C-C bond is more stable than C-N bond.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The linkage through oxygen results in ____ while through nitrogen atom, it leads to ____.
cards.back: The linkage through oxygen results in alkyl nitrites while through nitrogen atom, it leads to nitroalkanes.
cards.quote: The linkage through oxygen results in alkyl nitrites while through nitrogen atom, it leads to nitroalkanes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Who proposed the mechanism for an SN2 reaction, and in which year?
cards.back: In the year 1937, Edward Davies Hughes and Sir Christopher Ingold
cards.quote: In the year 1937, Edward Davies Hughes and Sir Christopher Ingold proposed a mechanism for an SN2 reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In SN2 the configuration at carbon turns like an umbrella in a strong wind. What is this process called?
cards.back: inversion of configuration
cards.quote: As a result configuration is inverted, the configuration (See box) of carbon atom under attack inverts in much the same way as an umbrella is turned inside out when caught in a strong wind. This process is called as inversion of configuration.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define configuration.
cards.back: Spacial arrangement of functional groups around carbon is called its configuration.
cards.quote: Spacial arrangement of functional groups around carbon is called its configuration.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Order of reactivity of alkyl halides in SN2 reactions?
cards.back: Primary halide > Secondary halide > Tertiary halide.
cards.quote: Thus the order of reactivity followed is: Primary halide > Secondary halide > Tertiary halide.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: SN1 reactions are generally carried out in ____ (like water, alcohol, acetic acid, etc.).
cards.back: SN1 reactions are generally carried out in polar protic solvents (like water, alcohol, acetic acid, etc.).
cards.quote: SN1 reactions are generally carried out in polar protic solvents (like water, alcohol, acetic acid, etc.).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Further, greater the ____, greater will be its ease of formation from alkyl halide and faster will be the rate of reaction.
cards.back: Further, greater the stability of carbocation, greater will be its ease of formation from alkyl halide and faster will be the rate of reaction.
cards.quote: Further, greater the stability of carbocation, greater will be its ease of formation from alkyl halide and faster will be the rate of reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: For a given alkyl group, the order of reactivity of R-X in both SN1 and SN2?
cards.back: R-I> R-Br>R-Cl>>R-F
cards.quote: For a given alkyl group, the reactivity of the halide, R-X, follows the same order in both the mechanisms R-I> R-Br>R-Cl>>R-F.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define optically active compounds.
cards.back: Plane of plane polarised light produced by passing ordinary light through Nicol prism is rotated when it is passed through the solutions of certain compounds. Such compounds are called optically active compounds.
cards.quote: Plane of plane polarised light produced by passing ordinary light through Nicol prism is rotated when it is passed through the solutions of certain compounds. Such compounds are called optically active compounds.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (i) Optical activity

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The angle by which the plane polarised light is rotated is measured by an instrument called ____.
cards.back: The angle by which the plane polarised light is rotated is measured by an instrument called polarimeter.
cards.quote: The angle by which the plane polarised light is rotated is measured by an instrument called polarimeter.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (i) Optical activity

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define dextrorotatory (d-form).
cards.back: If the compound rotates the plane of plane polarised light to the right, i.e., clockwise direction, it is called dextrorotatory (Greek for right rotating) or the d-form and is indicated by placing a positive (+) sign before the degree of rotation.
cards.quote: If the compound rotates the plane of plane polarised light to the right, i.e., clockwise direction, it is called dextrorotatory (Greek for right rotating) or the d-form and is indicated by placing a positive (+) sign before the degree of rotation.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (i) Optical activity

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define laevo-rotatory (l-form).
cards.back: If the light is rotated towards left (anticlockwise direction), the compound is said to be laevo-rotatory or the l-form and a negative (-) sign is placed before the degree of rotation.
cards.quote: If the light is rotated towards left (anticlockwise direction), the compound is said to be laevo-rotatory or the l-form and a negative (-) sign is placed before the degree of rotation.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (i) Optical activity

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are the (+) and (-) isomers of a compound called, and what is the phenomenon termed?
cards.back: optical isomers and the phenomenon is termed as optical isomerism.
cards.quote: Such (+) and (-) isomers of a compound are called optical isomers and the phenomenon is termed as optical isomerism.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (i) Optical activity

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The observation of ____ (____) that crystals of certain compounds exist in the form of mirror images laid the foundation of modern stereochemistry.
cards.back: The observation of Louis Pasteur (1848) that crystals of certain compounds exist in the form of mirror images laid the foundation of modern stereochemistry.
cards.quote: The observation of Louis Pasteur (1848) that crystals of certain compounds exist in the form of mirror images laid the foundation of modern stereochemistry.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define asymmetric carbon (stereocentre).
cards.back: if all the substituents attached to that carbon are different, the mirror image of the molecule is not superimposed (overlapped) on the molecule; such a carbon is called asymmetric carbon or stereocentre.
cards.quote: if all the substituents attached to that carbon are different, the mirror image of the molecule is not superimposed (overlapped) on the molecule; such a carbon is called asymmetric carbon or stereocentre.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The ____ of the molecule along with ____ of mirror images is responsible for the optical activity in such organic compounds.
cards.back: The asymmetry of the molecule along with non superimposability of mirror images is responsible for the optical activity in such organic compounds.
cards.quote: The asymmetry of the molecule along with non superimposability of mirror images is responsible for the optical activity in such organic compounds.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define chiral objects and chirality.
cards.back: The objects which are nonsuperimposable on their mirror image (like a pair of hands) are said to be chiral and this property is known as chirality.
cards.quote: The objects which are nonsuperimposable on their mirror image (like a pair of hands) are said to be chiral and this property is known as chirality.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chiral molecules are ____, while the objects, which are, superimposable on their mirror images are called ____.
cards.back: Chiral molecules are optically active, while the objects, which are, superimposable on their mirror images are called achiral.
cards.quote: Chiral molecules are optically active, while the objects, which are, superimposable on their mirror images are called achiral.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Butan-2-ol has ____ attached to the tetrahedral carbon and as expected is chiral.
cards.back: Butan-2-ol has four different groups attached to the tetrahedral carbon and as expected is chiral.
cards.quote: Butan-2-ol has four different groups attached to the tetrahedral carbon and as expected is chiral.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define enantiomers.
cards.back: The stereoisomers related to each other as non-superimposable mirror images are called enantiomers (Fig. 6.7).
cards.quote: The stereoisomers related to each other as non-superimposable mirror images are called enantiomers (Fig. 6.7).

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Enantiomers possess ____ namely, melting point, boiling point, refractive index, etc.
cards.back: Enantiomers possess identical physical properties namely, melting point, boiling point, refractive index, etc.
cards.quote: Enantiomers possess identical physical properties namely, melting point, boiling point, refractive index, etc.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define racemic mixture (racemic modification).
cards.back: A mixture containing two enantiomers in equal proportions will have zero optical rotation, as the rotation due to one isomer will be cancelled by the rotation due to the other isomer. Such a mixture is known as racemic mixture or racemic modification.
cards.quote: A mixture containing two enantiomers in equal proportions will have zero optical rotation, as the rotation due to one isomer will be cancelled by the rotation due to the other isomer. Such a mixture is known as racemic mixture or racemic modification.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A racemic mixture is represented by prefixing ____ or (±) before the name, for example (±) butan-2-ol.
cards.back: A racemic mixture is represented by prefixing dl or (±) before the name, for example (±) butan-2-ol.
cards.quote: A racemic mixture is represented by prefixing dl or (±) before the name, for example (±) butan-2-ol.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define racemisation.
cards.back: The process of conversion of enantiomer into a racemic mixture is known as racemisation.
cards.quote: The process of conversion of enantiomer into a racemic mixture is known as racemisation.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (ii) Molecular asymmetry, chirality and enantiomers

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define retention of configuration.
cards.back: Retention of configuration is the preservation of the spatial arrangement of bonds to an asymmetric centre during a chemical reaction or transformation.
cards.quote: Retention of configuration is the preservation of the spatial arrangement of bonds to an asymmetric centre during a chemical reaction or transformation.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (iii) Retention

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the three outcomes of a reaction at an asymmetric carbon when a bond to it is broken.
cards.back:
Inversion
retention
racemisation
cards.quote: Inversion, retention and racemisation: There are three outcomes for a reaction at an asymmetric carbon atom, when a bond directly linked to an asymmetric carbon atom is broken.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (iv) Inversion, retention and racemisation

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In case of optically active alkyl halides, the product formed as a result of SN2 mechanism has the ____ as compared to the reactant.
cards.back: In case of optically active alkyl halides, the product formed as a result of SN2 mechanism has the inverted configuration as compared to the reactant.
cards.quote: In case of optically active alkyl halides, the product formed as a result of SN2 mechanism has the inverted configuration as compared to the reactant.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (iv) Inversion, retention and racemisation

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In case of optically active alkyl halides, SN1 reactions are accompanied by ____.
cards.back: In case of optically active alkyl halides, SN1 reactions are accompanied by racemisation.
cards.quote: In case of optically active alkyl halides, SN1 reactions are accompanied by racemisation.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (iv) Inversion, retention and racemisation

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Actually the carbocation formed in the slow step being ____ is ____ (achiral).
cards.back: Actually the carbocation formed in the slow step being sp2 hybridised is planar (achiral).
cards.quote: Actually the carbocation formed in the slow step being sp2 hybridised is planar (achiral).

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: (c) Stereochemical aspects of nucleophilic substitution reactions: (iv) Inversion, retention and racemisation

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which Russian chemist formulated, in 1875, the rule for the preferred alkene in elimination?
cards.back: Russian chemist, Alexander Zaitsev (also pronounced as Saytzeff)
cards.quote: These form part of a pattern first observed by Russian chemist, Alexander Zaitsev (also pronounced as Saytzeff) who in 1875 formulated a rule

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: State Zaitsev (Saytzeff) rule.
cards.back: in dehydrohalogenation reactions, the preferred product is that alkene which has the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms.
cards.quote: in dehydrohalogenation reactions, the preferred product is that alkene which has the greater number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which route does a primary alkyl halide prefer with a base or nucleophile?
cards.back: a primary alkyl halide will prefer a SN2 reaction
cards.quote: Similarly, a primary alkyl halide will prefer a SN2 reaction, a secondary halide- SN2 or elimination depending upon the strength of base/nucleophile and a tertiary halide- SN1 or elimination depending upon the stability of carbocation or the more substituted alkene.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 2. Elimination reactions: Elimination versus substitution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define organo-metallic compounds.
cards.back: Most organic chlorides, bromides and iodides react with certain metals to give compounds containing carbon-metal bonds. Such compounds are known as organo-metallic compounds.
cards.quote: Most organic chlorides, bromides and iodides react with certain metals to give compounds containing carbon-metal bonds. Such compounds are known as organo-metallic compounds.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: An important class of organo-metallic compounds discovered by ____ in ____ is alkyl magnesium halide, RMgX, referred as Grignard Reagents.
cards.back: An important class of organo-metallic compounds discovered by Victor Grignard in 1900 is alkyl magnesium halide, RMgX, referred as Grignard Reagents.
cards.quote: An important class of organo-metallic compounds discovered by Victor Grignard in 1900 is alkyl magnesium halide, RMgX, referred as Grignard Reagents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Grignard reagents are highly reactive and react with any source of proton to give ____.
cards.back: Grignard reagents are highly reactive and react with any source of proton to give hydrocarbons.
cards.quote: Grignard reagents are highly reactive and react with any source of proton to give hydrocarbons.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: C-Cl bond acquires a ____ due to resonance.
cards.back: C-Cl bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance.
cards.quote: C-Cl bond acquires a partial double bond character due to resonance.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 1. Nucleophilic substitution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In case of haloarenes, the phenyl cation formed as a result of self-ionisation will not be stabilised by resonance and therefore, ____ is ruled out.
cards.back: In case of haloarenes, the phenyl cation formed as a result of self-ionisation will not be stabilised by resonance and therefore, SN1 mechanism is ruled out.
cards.quote: In case of haloarenes, the phenyl cation formed as a result of self-ionisation will not be stabilised by resonance and therefore, SN1 mechanism is ruled out.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 1. Nucleophilic substitution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chlorobenzene can be converted into phenol by heating in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution at a temperature of ____ and a pressure of ____.
cards.back: Chlorobenzene can be converted into phenol by heating in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution at a temperature of 623K and a pressure of 300 atmospheres.
cards.quote: Chlorobenzene can be converted into phenol by heating in aqueous sodium hydroxide solution at a temperature of 623K and a pressure of 300 atmospheres.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 1. Nucleophilic substitution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The presence of an electron withdrawing group (-NO2) at ____ increases the reactivity of haloarenes.
cards.back: The presence of an electron withdrawing group (-NO2) at ortho- and para-positions increases the reactivity of haloarenes.
cards.quote: The presence of an electron withdrawing group (-NO2) at ortho- and para-positions increases the reactivity of haloarenes.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 1. Nucleophilic substitution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the usual electrophilic reactions of the benzene ring that haloarenes undergo.
cards.back:
halogenation
nitration
sulphonation
Friedel-Crafts reactions
cards.quote: Haloarenes undergo the usual electrophilic reactions of the benzene ring such as halogenation, nitration, sulphonation and Friedel-Crafts reactions.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 2. Electrophilic substitution reactions

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Halogen atom besides being ____ is ____; therefore, further substitution occurs at ortho- and para-positions with respect to the halogen atom.
cards.back: Halogen atom besides being slightly deactivating is o, p-directing; therefore, further substitution occurs at ortho- and para-positions with respect to the halogen atom.
cards.quote: Halogen atom besides being slightly deactivating is o, p-directing; therefore, further substitution occurs at ortho- and para-positions with respect to the halogen atom.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 2. Electrophilic substitution reactions

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why do electrophilic substitution reactions in haloarenes occur slowly?
cards.back: the ring gets somewhat deactivated as compared to benzene and hence the electrophilic substitution reactions in haloarenes occur slowly and require more drastic conditions as compared to those in benzene.
cards.quote: As a result, the ring gets somewhat deactivated as compared to benzene and hence the electrophilic substitution reactions in haloarenes occur slowly and require more drastic conditions as compared to those in benzene.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 2. Electrophilic substitution reactions

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chlorine ____ through inductive effect and ____ through resonance.
cards.back: Chlorine withdraws electrons through inductive effect and releases electrons through resonance.
cards.quote: Chlorine withdraws electrons through inductive effect and releases electrons through resonance.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: Example 6.9

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Reactivity is thus controlled by the ____ and orientation is controlled by resonance effect.
cards.back: Reactivity is thus controlled by the stronger inductive effect and orientation is controlled by resonance effect.
cards.quote: Reactivity is thus controlled by the stronger inductive effect and orientation is controlled by resonance effect.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: Example 6.9

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A mixture of an alkyl halide and aryl halide gives an alkylarene when treated with sodium in dry ether and is called ____.
cards.back: A mixture of an alkyl halide and aryl halide gives an alkylarene when treated with sodium in dry ether and is called Wurtz-Fittig reaction.
cards.quote: A mixture of an alkyl halide and aryl halide gives an alkylarene when treated with sodium in dry ether and is called Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 3. Reaction with metals

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Aryl halides also give analogous compounds when treated with sodium in dry ether, in which two aryl groups are joined together. It is called ____.
cards.back: Aryl halides also give analogous compounds when treated with sodium in dry ether, in which two aryl groups are joined together. It is called Fittig reaction.
cards.quote: Aryl halides also give analogous compounds when treated with sodium in dry ether, in which two aryl groups are joined together. It is called Fittig reaction.

source.section: 6.7 Chemical Reactions: 6.7.2 Reactions of Haloarenes: 3. Reaction with metals

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define polyhalogen compounds.
cards.back: Carbon compounds containing more than one halogen atom are usually referred to as polyhalogen compounds.
cards.quote: Carbon compounds containing more than one halogen atom are usually referred to as polyhalogen compounds.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent as a ____, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.
cards.back: Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent as a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.
cards.quote: Dichloromethane is widely used as a solvent as a paint remover, as a propellant in aerosols, and as a process solvent in the manufacture of drugs.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chemically, chloroform is employed as a solvent for fats, ____, iodine and other substances.
cards.back: Chemically, chloroform is employed as a solvent for fats, alkaloids, iodine and other substances.
cards.quote: Chemically, chloroform is employed as a solvent for fats, alkaloids, iodine and other substances.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The major use of chloroform today is in the production of the freon refrigerant ____.
cards.back: The major use of chloroform today is in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22.
cards.quote: The major use of chloroform today is in the production of the freon refrigerant R-22.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in the presence of light to an extremely poisonous gas, ____, also known as ____.
cards.back: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in the presence of light to an extremely poisonous gas, carbonyl chloride, also known as phosgene.
cards.quote: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air in the presence of light to an extremely poisonous gas, carbonyl chloride, also known as phosgene.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Iodoform (triiodomethane) was used as an antiseptic. What causes its antiseptic action?
cards.back: the antiseptic properties are due to the liberation of free iodine and not due to iodoform itself.
cards.quote: It was used earlier as an antiseptic but the antiseptic properties are due to the liberation of free iodine and not due to iodoform itself.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: There is some evidence that exposure to carbon tetrachloride causes ____ in humans.
cards.back: There is some evidence that exposure to carbon tetrachloride causes liver cancer in humans.
cards.quote: There is some evidence that exposure to carbon tetrachloride causes liver cancer in humans.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When carbon tetrachloride is released into the air, it rises to the atmosphere and depletes the ____.
cards.back: When carbon tetrachloride is released into the air, it rises to the atmosphere and depletes the ozone layer.
cards.quote: When carbon tetrachloride is released into the air, it rises to the atmosphere and depletes the ozone layer.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define freons.
cards.back: The chlorofluorocarbon compounds of methane and ethane are collectively known as freons.
cards.quote: The chlorofluorocarbon compounds of methane and ethane are collectively known as freons.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the properties of freons.
cards.back:
extremely stable
unreactive
non-toxic
noncorrosive
easily liquefiable gases
cards.quote: They are extremely stable, unreactive, non-toxic, noncorrosive and easily liquefiable gases.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Freon 12 (CCl2F2) is manufactured from tetrachloromethane by which reaction?
cards.back: It is manufactured from tetrachloromethane by Swarts reaction.
cards.quote: Freon 12 (CCl2F2) is one of the most common freons in industrial use. It is manufactured from tetrachloromethane by Swarts reaction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In stratosphere, freon is able to initiate ____ that can upset the natural ____.
cards.back: In stratosphere, freon is able to initiate radical chain reactions that can upset the natural ozone balance.
cards.quote: In stratosphere, freon is able to initiate radical chain reactions that can upset the natural ozone balance.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: DDT is not metabolised very rapidly by animals; instead, it is deposited and stored in the ____.
cards.back: DDT is not metabolised very rapidly by animals; instead, it is deposited and stored in the fatty tissues.
cards.quote: DDT is not metabolised very rapidly by animals; instead, it is deposited and stored in the fatty tissues.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The use of DDT was banned in the United States in ____, although it is still in use in some other parts of the world.
cards.back: The use of DDT was banned in the United States in 1973, although it is still in use in some other parts of the world.
cards.quote: The use of DDT was banned in the United States in 1973, although it is still in use in some other parts of the world.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Fluorides and iodides are best prepared by ____.
cards.back: Fluorides and iodides are best prepared by halogen exchange method.
cards.quote: Fluorides and iodides are best prepared by halogen exchange method.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define a solution (NCERT).
cards.back: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more than two components.
cards.quote: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures of two or more than two components.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: By homogenous mixture we mean that its composition and properties are ____ throughout the mixture.
cards.back: By homogenous mixture we mean that its composition and properties are uniform throughout the mixture.
cards.quote: By homogenous mixture we mean that its composition and properties are uniform throughout the mixture.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which component of a solution is known as the solvent?
cards.back: Generally, the component that is present in the largest quantity is known as solvent.
cards.quote: Generally, the component that is present in the largest quantity is known as solvent.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Solvent determines the ____ in which solution exists.
cards.back: Solvent determines the physical state in which solution exists.
cards.quote: Solvent determines the physical state in which solution exists.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are solutes?
cards.back: One or more components present in the solution other than solvent are called solutes.
cards.quote: One or more components present in the solution other than solvent are called solutes.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 1.1: NCERT's example of a gaseous solution with a gas solute in a gas solvent.
cards.back: Mixture of oxygen and nitrogen gases
cards.quote: Gas Gas Mixture of oxygen and nitrogen gases

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 1.1: NCERT's example of a gaseous solution with a solid solute in a gas solvent.
cards.back: Camphor in nitrogen gas
cards.quote: Solid Gas Camphor in nitrogen gas

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 1.1 examples of liquid solutions (solute: gas, liquid, solid).
cards.back:
Oxygen dissolved in water
Ethanol dissolved in water
Glucose dissolved in water
cards.quote: Oxygen dissolved in water Ethanol dissolved in water Glucose dissolved in water

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Table 1.1 examples of solid solutions (solute: gas, liquid, solid).
cards.back:
Solution of hydrogen in palladium
Amalgam of mercury with sodium
Copper dissolved in gold
cards.quote: Solution of hydrogen in palladium Amalgam of mercury with sodium Copper dissolved in gold

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: NCERT's solid solution in which the solute is a gas (Table 1.1).
cards.back: Solution of hydrogen in palladium
cards.quote: Solution of hydrogen in palladium Amalgam of mercury with sodium Copper dissolved in gold

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A solution is described as 10% glucose in water by mass. What does it mean?
cards.back: it means that 10 g of glucose is dissolved in 90 g of water resulting in a 100 g solution.
cards.quote: if a solution is described by 10% glucose in water by mass, it means that 10 g of glucose is dissolved in 90 g of water resulting in a 100 g solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does a 10% ethanol solution in water (by volume) mean?
cards.back: 10 mL of ethanol is dissolved in water such that the total volume of the solution is 100 mL.
cards.quote: 10% ethanol solution in water means that 10 mL of ethanol is dissolved in water such that the total volume of the solution is 100 mL.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is mass by volume percentage (w/V), commonly used in medicine and pharmacy?
cards.back: Another unit which is commonly used in medicine and pharmacy is mass by volume percentage. It is the mass of solute dissolved in 100 mL of the solution.
cards.quote: Another unit which is commonly used in medicine and pharmacy is mass by volume percentage. It is the mass of solute dissolved in 100 mL of the solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: When a solute is present in trace quantities, it is convenient to express concentration in ____ (ppm)
cards.back: When a solute is present in trace quantities, it is convenient to express concentration in parts per million (ppm)
cards.quote: When a solute is present in trace quantities, it is convenient to express concentration in parts per million (ppm)

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: mole fraction of a component.
cards.back: Mole fraction of a component = Number of moles of the component / Total number of moles of all the components
cards.quote: Mole fraction of a component = Number of moles of the component Total number of moles of all the components

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define molarity (M).
cards.back: Molarity (M) is defined as number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre (or one cubic decimetre) of solution
cards.quote: Molarity (M) is defined as number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre (or one cubic decimetre) of solution

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does a 0.25 M solution of NaOH mean?
cards.back: 0.25 mol of NaOH has been dissolved in one litre (or one cubic decimetre).
cards.quote: 0.25 mol L–1 (or 0.25 M) solution of NaOH means that 0.25 mol of NaOH has been dissolved in one litre (or one cubic decimetre).

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define molality (m).
cards.back: Molality (m) is defined as the number of moles of the solute per kilogram (kg) of the solvent
cards.quote: Molality (m) is defined as the number of moles of the solute per kilogram (kg) of the solvent

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: molality (m).
cards.back: Molality (m) = Moles of solute / Mass of solvent in kg
cards.quote: Molality (m) = Moles of solute Mass of solvent in kg

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What does a 1.00 m solution of KCl mean?
cards.back: 1 mol (74.5 g) of KCl is dissolved in 1 kg of water.
cards.quote: 1.00 mol kg–1 (or 1.00 m) solution of KCl means that 1 mol (74.5 g) of KCl is dissolved in 1 kg of water.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Mass %, ppm, mole fraction and molality are independent of temperature, whereas ____ is a function of temperature.
cards.back: Mass %, ppm, mole fraction and molality are independent of temperature, whereas molarity is a function of temperature.
cards.quote: Mass %, ppm, mole fraction and molality are independent of temperature, whereas molarity is a function of temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define the solubility of a substance.
cards.back: Solubility of a substance is its maximum amount that can be dissolved in a specified amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
cards.quote: Solubility of a substance is its maximum amount that can be dissolved in a specified amount of solvent at a specified temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which solutes dissolve in polar solvents, and which in nonpolar solvents?
cards.back: polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents and non polar solutes in nonpolar solvents.
cards.quote: It is observed that polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents and non polar solutes in nonpolar solvents.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In general, a solute dissolves in a solvent if the intermolecular interactions are similar in the two or we may say ____.
cards.back: In general, a solute dissolves in a solvent if the intermolecular interactions are similar in the two or we may say like dissolves like.
cards.quote: In general, a solute dissolves in a solvent if the intermolecular interactions are similar in the two or we may say like dissolves like.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the process called when a solid solute added to a solvent dissolves and its concentration increases?
cards.back: When a solid solute is added to the solvent, some solute dissolves and its concentration increases in solution. This process is known as dissolution.
cards.quote: When a solid solute is added to the solvent, some solute dissolves and its concentration increases in solution. This process is known as dissolution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the process called when solute particles in solution collide with solid solute and get separated out?
cards.back: Some solute particles in solution collide with the solid solute particles and get separated out of solution. This process is known as crystallisation.
cards.quote: Some solute particles in solution collide with the solid solute particles and get separated out of solution. This process is known as crystallisation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a saturated solution?
cards.back: Such a solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature and pressure is called a saturated solution.
cards.quote: Such a solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature and pressure is called a saturated solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is an unsaturated solution?
cards.back: An unsaturated solution is one in which more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature.
cards.quote: An unsaturated solution is one in which more solute can be dissolved at the same temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Pressure does not have any significant effect on solubility of ____.
cards.back: Pressure does not have any significant effect on solubility of solids in liquids.
cards.quote: Pressure does not have any significant effect on solubility of solids in liquids.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How does the solubility of gases in liquids change with pressure?
cards.back: The solubility of gases increase with increase of pressure.
cards.quote: The solubility of gases increase with increase of pressure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: State Henry's law (solubility form).
cards.back: The law states that at a constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of liquid or solution.
cards.quote: The law states that at a constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of liquid or solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: Henry's law (partial pressure form).
cards.back: p = KH x
cards.quote: The most commonly used form of Henry's law states that "the partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase (p) is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas (x) in the solution" and is expressed as: p = KH x

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In Henry's law, p = KH x, what is KH?
cards.back: Here KH is the Henry's law constant.
cards.quote: Here KH is the Henry's law constant.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why is a soda water bottle sealed under high pressure?
cards.back: To increase the solubility of CO2 in soft drinks and soda water, the bottle is sealed under high pressure.
cards.quote: To increase the solubility of CO2 in soft drinks and soda water, the bottle is sealed under high pressure.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: How does the solubility of gases in liquids change with rise in temperature?
cards.back: Solubility of gases in liquids decreases with rise in temperature.
cards.quote: Solubility of gases in liquids decreases with rise in temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: State Raoult's law for a solution of volatile liquids.
cards.back: the partial vapour pressure of each component of the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution.
cards.quote: the partial vapour pressure of each component of the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Raoult's law is a special case of which law?
cards.back: Raoult's law becomes a special case of Henry's law
cards.quote: Thus, Raoult's law becomes a special case of Henry's law

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define vapour pressure (NCERT).
cards.back: Liquids at a given temperature vapourise and under equilibrium conditions the pressure exerted by the vapours of the liquid over the liquid phase is called vapour pressure
cards.quote: Liquids at a given temperature vapourise and under equilibrium conditions the pressure exerted by the vapours of the liquid over the liquid phase is called vapour pressure

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The decrease in the vapour pressure of solvent depends on the quantity of non-volatile solute present in the solution, ____.
cards.back: The decrease in the vapour pressure of solvent depends on the quantity of non-volatile solute present in the solution, irrespective of its nature.
cards.quote: The decrease in the vapour pressure of solvent depends on the quantity of non-volatile solute present in the solution, irrespective of its nature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Adding 1.0 mol of sucrose vs 1.0 mol of urea to one kg of water: how do the vapour pressure decreases compare?
cards.back: nearly similar to that produced by adding 1.0 mol of urea to the same quantity of water at the same temperature.
cards.quote: decrease in the vapour pressure of water by adding 1.0 mol of sucrose to one kg of water is nearly similar to that produced by adding 1.0 mol of urea to the same quantity of water at the same temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: State Raoult's law in its general form.
cards.back: Raoult's law in its general form can be stated as, for any solution the partial vapour pressure of each volatile component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction.
cards.quote: Raoult's law in its general form can be stated as, for any solution the partial vapour pressure of each volatile component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are ideal solutions?
cards.back: The solutions which obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration are known as ideal solutions.
cards.quote: The solutions which obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration are known as ideal solutions.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the two other important properties of ideal solutions.
cards.back:
The enthalpy of mixing of the pure components to form the solution is zero
the volume of mixing is also zero
cards.quote: The enthalpy of mixing of the pure components to form the solution is zero and the volume of mixing is also zero

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: If the intermolecular attractive forces between the A-A and B-B are ____ to those between A-B, this leads to the formation of ideal solution.
cards.back: If the intermolecular attractive forces between the A-A and B-B are nearly equal to those between A-B, this leads to the formation of ideal solution.
cards.quote: If the intermolecular attractive forces between the A-A and B-B are nearly equal to those between A-B, this leads to the formation of ideal solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the pairs NCERT gives as nearly ideal solutions.
cards.back:
n-hexane and n-heptane
bromoethane and chloroethane
benzene and toluene
cards.quote: Solution of n-hexane and n-heptane, bromoethane and chloroethane, benzene and toluene, etc. fall into this category.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a non-ideal solution?
cards.back: When a solution does not obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration, then it is called non-ideal solution.
cards.quote: When a solution does not obey Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration, then it is called non-ideal solution.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: If it is higher, the solution exhibits ____ deviation and if it is lower, it exhibits ____ deviation from Raoult's law.
cards.back: If it is higher, the solution exhibits positive deviation and if it is lower, it exhibits negative deviation from Raoult's law.
cards.quote: If it is higher, the solution exhibits positive deviation and if it is lower, it exhibits negative deviation from Raoult's law.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In case of positive deviation from Raoult's law, A-B interactions are ____ than those between A-A or B-B
cards.back: In case of positive deviation from Raoult's law, A-B interactions are weaker than those between A-A or B-B
cards.quote: In case of positive deviation from Raoult's law, A-B interactions are weaker than those between A-A or B-B

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In pure ethanol, molecules are hydrogen bonded. What deviation from Raoult's law results on adding acetone, and why?
cards.back: On adding acetone, its molecules get in between the host molecules and break some of the hydrogen bonds between them. Due to weakening of interactions, the solution shows positive deviation from Raoult's law
cards.quote: In pure ethanol, molecules are hydrogen bonded. On adding acetone, its molecules get in between the host molecules and break some of the hydrogen bonds between them. Due to weakening of interactions, the solution shows positive deviation from Raoult's law

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Carbon disulphide added to acetone shows which deviation from Raoult's law, and why?
cards.back: the dipolar interactions between solute-solvent molecules are weaker than the respective interactions among the solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecules. This solution also shows positive deviation.
cards.quote: In a solution formed by adding carbon disulphide to acetone, the dipolar interactions between solute-solvent molecules are weaker than the respective interactions among the solute-solute and solvent-solvent molecules. This solution also shows positive deviation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A mixture of chloroform and acetone shows which deviation from Raoult's law?
cards.back: a mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law.
cards.quote: Similarly, a mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are azeotropes?
cards.back: Some liquids on mixing, form azeotropes which are binary mixtures having the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
cards.quote: Some liquids on mixing, form azeotropes which are binary mixtures having the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Types of azeotropes.
cards.back:
minimum boiling azeotrope
maximum boiling azeotrope
cards.quote: There are two types of azeotropes called minimum boiling azeotrope and maximum boiling azeotrope.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The solutions which show a large positive deviation from Raoult's law form ____ at a specific composition.
cards.back: The solutions which show a large positive deviation from Raoult's law form minimum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition.
cards.quote: The solutions which show a large positive deviation from Raoult's law form minimum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Fractional distillation of an ethanol-water mixture gives a solution of approximately what composition?
cards.back: a solution containing approximately 95% by volume of ethanol.
cards.quote: For example, ethanol-water mixture (obtained by fermentation of sugars) on fractional distillation gives a solution containing approximately 95% by volume of ethanol.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The solutions that show large negative deviation from Raoult's law form ____ at a specific composition.
cards.back: The solutions that show large negative deviation from Raoult's law form maximum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition.
cards.quote: The solutions that show large negative deviation from Raoult's law form maximum boiling azeotrope at a specific composition.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Nitric acid and water form a maximum boiling azeotrope: approximate composition and boiling point?
cards.back: approximate composition, 68% nitric acid and 32% water by mass, with a boiling point of 393.5 K.
cards.quote: This azeotrope has the approximate composition, 68% nitric acid and 32% water by mass, with a boiling point of 393.5 K.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are colligative properties?
cards.back: All these properties depend on the number of solute particles irrespective of their nature relative to the total number of particles present in the solution. Such properties are called colligative properties
cards.quote: All these properties depend on the number of solute particles irrespective of their nature relative to the total number of particles present in the solution. Such properties are called colligative properties

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Name the four colligative properties.
cards.back:
relative lowering of vapour pressure of the solvent
depression of freezing point of the solvent
elevation of boiling point of the solvent
osmotic pressure of the solution
cards.quote: These are: (1) relative lowering of vapour pressure of the solvent (2) depression of freezing point of the solvent (3) elevation of boiling point of the solvent and (4) osmotic pressure of the solution.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Raoult established that the lowering of vapour pressure depends only on the concentration of the solute particles and it is ____ of their identity.
cards.back: Raoult established that the lowering of vapour pressure depends only on the concentration of the solute particles and it is independent of their identity.
cards.quote: Raoult established that the lowering of vapour pressure depends only on the concentration of the solute particles and it is independent of their identity.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is the relative lowering of vapour pressure equal to?
cards.back: The expression on the left hand side of the equation as mentioned earlier is called relative lowering of vapour pressure and is equal to the mole fraction of the solute.
cards.quote: The expression on the left hand side of the equation as mentioned earlier is called relative lowering of vapour pressure and is equal to the mole fraction of the solute.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why does water boil at 373.15 K (100° C)?
cards.back: at this temperature the vapour pressure of water is 1.013 bar (1 atmosphere).
cards.quote: water boils at 373.15 K (100° C) because at this temperature the vapour pressure of water is 1.013 bar (1 atmosphere).

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is Kb called?
cards.back: Kb is called Boiling Point Elevation Constant or Molal Elevation Constant (Ebullioscopic Constant).
cards.quote: Kb is called Boiling Point Elevation Constant or Molal Elevation Constant (Ebullioscopic Constant).

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define the freezing point of a substance (NCERT).
cards.back: the freezing point of a substance may be defined as the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the substance in its liquid phase is equal to its vapour pressure in the solid phase.
cards.quote: the freezing point of a substance may be defined as the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the substance in its liquid phase is equal to its vapour pressure in the solid phase.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is Kf called?
cards.back: The proportionality constant, Kf, which depends on the nature of the solvent is known as Freezing Point Depression Constant or Molal Depression Constant or Cryoscopic Constant.
cards.quote: The proportionality constant, Kf, which depends on the nature of the solvent is known as Freezing Point Depression Constant or Molal Depression Constant or Cryoscopic Constant.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are semipermeable membranes (SPM)?
cards.back: Small solvent molecules, like water, can pass through these holes but the passage of bigger molecules like solute is hindered. Membranes having this kind of properties are known as semipermeable membranes (SPM).
cards.quote: Small solvent molecules, like water, can pass through these holes but the passage of bigger molecules like solute is hindered. Membranes having this kind of properties are known as semipermeable membranes (SPM).

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is osmosis?
cards.back: the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent to the solution. This process of flow of the solvent is called osmosis.
cards.quote: the solvent molecules will flow through the membrane from pure solvent to the solution. This process of flow of the solvent is called osmosis.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The important point to be kept in mind is that solvent molecules always flow from ____ to ____ of solution.
cards.back: The important point to be kept in mind is that solvent molecules always flow from lower concentration to higher concentration of solution.
cards.quote: The important point to be kept in mind is that solvent molecules always flow from lower concentration to higher concentration of solution.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define the osmotic pressure of a solution.
cards.back: The osmotic pressure of a solution is the excess pressure that must be applied to a solution to prevent osmosis, i.e., to stop the passage of solvent molecules through a semipermeable membrane into the solution.
cards.quote: The osmotic pressure of a solution is the excess pressure that must be applied to a solution to prevent osmosis, i.e., to stop the passage of solvent molecules through a semipermeable membrane into the solution.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: The osmotic pressure method has the advantage over other methods as pressure measurement is around the ____
cards.back: The osmotic pressure method has the advantage over other methods as pressure measurement is around the room temperature
cards.quote: The osmotic pressure method has the advantage over other methods as pressure measurement is around the room temperature

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What are isotonic solutions?
cards.back: Two solutions having same osmotic pressure at a given temperature are called isotonic solutions.
cards.quote: Two solutions having same osmotic pressure at a given temperature are called isotonic solutions.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which solution has osmotic pressure equivalent to the fluid inside the blood cell?
cards.back: 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride solution, called normal saline solution and it is safe to inject intravenously.
cards.quote: the osmotic pressure associated with the fluid inside the blood cell is equivalent to that of 0.9% (mass/volume) sodium chloride solution, called normal saline solution and it is safe to inject intravenously.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a hypertonic solution (relative to blood cells)?
cards.back: if we place the cells in a solution containing more than 0.9% (mass/ volume) sodium chloride, water will flow out of the cells and they would shrink. Such a solution is called hypertonic.
cards.quote: if we place the cells in a solution containing more than 0.9% (mass/ volume) sodium chloride, water will flow out of the cells and they would shrink. Such a solution is called hypertonic.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is a hypotonic solution (relative to blood cells)?
cards.back: If the salt concentration is less than 0.9% (mass/ volume), the solution is said to be hypotonic. In this case, water will flow into the cells if placed in this solution and they would swell.
cards.quote: If the salt concentration is less than 0.9% (mass/ volume), the solution is said to be hypotonic. In this case, water will flow into the cells if placed in this solution and they would swell.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: A raw mango is placed in concentrated salt solution. What happens, and by which process?
cards.back: A raw mango placed in concentrated salt solution loses water via osmosis and shrivel into pickle.
cards.quote: A raw mango placed in concentrated salt solution loses water via osmosis and shrivel into pickle.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: What is reverse osmosis?
cards.back: The direction of osmosis can be reversed if a pressure larger than the osmotic pressure is applied to the solution side. That is, now the pure solvent flows out of the solution through the semi permeable membrane. This phenomenon is called reverse osmosis
cards.quote: The direction of osmosis can be reversed if a pressure larger than the osmotic pressure is applied to the solution side. That is, now the pure solvent flows out of the solution through the semi permeable membrane. This phenomenon is called reverse osmosis

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Reverse osmosis is used in ____ of sea water.
cards.back: Reverse osmosis is used in desalination of sea water.
cards.quote: Reverse osmosis is used in desalination of sea water.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which porous membrane is workable for reverse osmosis of sea water?
cards.back: A workable porous membrane is a film of cellulose acetate placed over a suitable support. Cellulose acetate is permeable to water but impermeable to impurities and ions present in sea water.
cards.quote: A workable porous membrane is a film of cellulose acetate placed over a suitable support. Cellulose acetate is permeable to water but impermeable to impurities and ions present in sea water.

source.section: 1.6 Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why do ethanoic acid molecules show abnormal molar mass in benzene?
cards.back: Molecules of ethanoic acid (acetic acid) dimerise in benzene due to hydrogen bonding. This normally happens in solvents of low dielectric constant. In this case the number of particles is reduced due to dimerisation.
cards.quote: Molecules of ethanoic acid (acetic acid) dimerise in benzene due to hydrogen bonding. This normally happens in solvents of low dielectric constant. In this case the number of particles is reduced due to dimerisation.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Why did van't Hoff introduce the factor i in 1880?
cards.back: In 1880 van't Hoff introduced a factor i, known as the van't Hoff factor, to account for the extent of dissociation or association.
cards.quote: In 1880 van't Hoff introduced a factor i, known as the van't Hoff factor, to account for the extent of dissociation or association.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: van't Hoff factor i (molar mass and colligative property form).
cards.back: i = Normal molar mass / Abnormal molar mass = Observed colligative property / Calculated colligative property
cards.quote: i Normal molar mass Abnormal molar mass Observed colligative property Calculated colligative property

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Formula: van't Hoff factor i (moles of particles form).
cards.back: i = Total number of moles of particles after association/dissociation / Number of moles of particles before association/dissociation
cards.quote: i Total number of moles of particles after association/dissociation Number of moles of particles before association/dissociation

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: In case of association, value of i is ____ than unity while for dissociation it is ____ than unity.
cards.back: In case of association, value of i is less than unity while for dissociation it is greater than unity.
cards.quote: In case of association, value of i is less than unity while for dissociation it is greater than unity.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Van't Hoff factor i: aqueous KCl solution versus ethanoic acid in benzene?
cards.back: the value of i for aqueous KCl solution is close to 2, while the value for ethanoic acid in benzene is nearly 0.5.
cards.quote: For example, the value of i for aqueous KCl solution is close to 2, while the value for ethanoic acid in benzene is nearly 0.5.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Which salts have i approaching 2 on dilution, and which has i close to 3?
cards.back: For KCl, NaCl and MgSO4, i values approach 2 as the solution becomes very dilute. As expected, the value of i gets close to 3 for K2SO4.
cards.quote: For KCl, NaCl and MgSO4, i values approach 2 as the solution becomes very dilute. As expected, the value of i gets close to 3 for K2SO4.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Types of solutions (NCERT summary).
cards.back:
solid
liquid
gaseous solutions
cards.quote: Solutions are classified as solid, liquid and gaseous solutions.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Azeotropes arise due to ____ from Raoult's law.
cards.back: Azeotropes arise due to very large deviations from Raoult's law.
cards.quote: Azeotropes arise due to very large deviations from Raoult's law.

cards.subject: chemistry
cards.front: Define the van't Hoff factor i (NCERT summary).
cards.back: This factor has been defined as ratio of normal molar mass to experimentally determined molar mass or as the ratio of observed colligative property to the calculated colligative property.
cards.quote: This factor has been defined as ratio of normal molar mass to experimentally determined molar mass or as the ratio of observed colligative property to the calculated colligative property.
